# Phases (spec-driven, acceptance tests first)

> Owner: Team lead · Read in: every phase · Agent: read-only

Run the phases in order. A phase starts only after the previous gate has passed.
Adds to `general/working-rules.md`; does not replace it. Path aliases: see `AGENTS.md`.

| # | Phase | Reads | Writes | Gate (must be true to continue) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Preflight & bootstrap | `project/00_setup/*`, `general/engineering-standards.md`, `general/security/security-baseline.md`, `general/quality/severity-scale.md`, skill `general/skills/preflight` | `docs/00_preflight-report.md`, `docs/00_input-manifest.sha256`, `docs/00_progress.md`, one skeleton per component, repo files (ES-03) | Every preflight check passes; every component builds; manifests and lock files match `tech-stack.md` exactly (as amended by approved decision records); every listed tool runs; input manifest written |
| 1 | Requirements | `project/01_requirements/*` (the acceptance criteria and end-to-end scenarios are inputs and are not changed) | `docs/01_requirements-check.md` (story → criteria; gaps only, nothing copied) | Every story has ≥ 1 AC in the given list; every AC cites a story; every open question has an answer in `scope.md`; a gap or contradiction in the inputs is a decision record |
| 2 | Design | `project/01_requirements/*`, `project/00_setup/tech-stack.md`, `project/00_setup/environments.md`, `project/02_design/*`, `general/security/*` | `docs/02_specification.md`, `docs/02_contracts/` | Every AC, SR, SB and NFR maps to the spec; contracts validate with a parser |
| 3 | Test design | `project/01_requirements/acceptance-criteria.md`, `project/01_requirements/e2e-scenarios.md`, `docs/02_contracts/`, `general/quality/test-strategy.md`, `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`, skill `general/skills/write-acceptance-tests` | acceptance tests, `docs/03_test-strategy.md`, `docs/03_acceptance-manifest.sha256` | Every AC has a test; every e2e scenario has exactly one e2e test and there is no other e2e test; every test fails for a behavioural reason (no build or setup errors), or passes only because bootstrap code already provides the behaviour, listed in `docs/03_test-strategy.md`; manifest committed last, after all tests, as its own freeze commit |
| 4 | Build | `docs/02_*`, `project/00_setup/tech-stack.md`, `project/00_setup/environments.md`, `project/02_design/architecture.md`, `general/engineering-standards.md` | source code | All frozen acceptance tests pass; format, lint and type checks are clean; at least one commit per user story |
| 5 | Unit tests | source code, `general/quality/test-strategy.md`, `general/quality/measurement-scope.md` | unit tests, `docs/03_test-strategy.md` | First full run recorded and classified before any fix; full suite passes; **quality gate** met for each component as `general/quality/measurement-scope.md` ("Quality gate") defines: line coverage and adjusted mutation score at or above the thresholds in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md`, or the shortfall recorded after the third survivor round; no further tests for a component once it meets the gate |
| 6 | Verify | all of `01_input/`, all of `docs/`, skill `general/skills/verify-release` | `docs/06_verification-report.md` | Every general and project DoD item has evidence; no open Critical/High finding; manifest hashes match; no secret value found in any file, log or commit message; coverage and mutation score re-measured only for a component whose code or tests changed since phase 5, once, after the last fix |
| 7 | Release | `general/quality/definition-of-done.md`, `general/engineering-standards.md`, `project/02_design/architecture.md` | `out/README.md`, one README per component, `docs/release-notes.md` | Every README works when followed from a clean checkout; manual-test list present; every decision has a resolution or is listed as pending review |

Any phase may write `docs/decisions-log.md`, `docs/00_progress.md` and `out/logs/`.

## On a failed gate

- Fix within the same phase, then re-check the gate.
- If the gate needs a change to an input or a frozen test, stop and raise a decision record.

## Test levels

| Level | Written in phase | Written from | Frozen | Location |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Acceptance | 3 | acceptance criteria + contracts | yes, from the freeze commit | path contains `acceptance` |
| End-to-end | 3 | `project/01_requirements/e2e-scenarios.md` (one test per scenario) | yes, from the freeze commit | path contains `e2e` |
| Unit / integration | 5 | implementation | no | any other test path |

## Commit units

| Phase | One commit per |
|---|---|
| 0 | component build file (pinned dependencies) and, separately, its source skeleton; repository files (ES-03); the preflight report, input manifest and progress file together (one commit) |
| 1, 2 | the requirements check (one commit); the specification with all its contracts (one commit) |
| 3 | user story's acceptance and end-to-end tests, then the freeze commit (manifest only) |
| 4 | layer of one user story (domain and use case, persistence or adapter, web/API, UI), each at most 15 files and 400 lines; the tests are already frozen, so no test or document in the same commit |
| 5 | group of test classes of one area or layer, at most 400 lines (for example domain rules, adapters, web filters, UI screen); tool configuration (Stryker, JaCoCo) in its own `build` commit |
| 6 | fix of one finding, with its re-run evidence; the report in its own commit |
| 7 | README, release notes |

## Constraints

- Do not read or write production source code in phase 3.
- Do not write unit tests before phase 5.
- Do not edit, delete or weaken a test listed in `docs/03_acceptance-manifest.sha256`.

## Evidence (checked in phase 6)

- The phase 3 commits add no production code beyond the bootstrap skeleton; the freeze commit adds the manifest, and every file it lists was committed earlier in phase 3.
- Build has at least one commit per user story, each naming its `US`/`AC` ID; no commit exceeds 15 files or 400 lines or mixes code, tests, documents and build files (`working-rules.md`, Commits). The report measures message length, bursts and size on every commit, so the agent does not audit commit subjects itself.
- Every hash in the manifest still matches.
----
# Working rules

> Owner: Team lead · Read in: every phase · Agent: read-only

## Ask the human (blocking)

Record a decision in `docs/decisions-log.md` (format under "Decision record"), ask, and wait when:

- anything checked in phase 0 is missing or wrong and only a human can fix it;
- a technology, version or service from `project/00_setup/tech-stack.md` does not work or needs changing;
- a frozen acceptance test appears wrong (only a human may update the manifest afterwards);
- a Critical or High finding would be downgraded or accepted.

Ask all open questions of a phase in one message. While waiting, finish work that does not depend on the answer.

## Decide and record (non-blocking)

When a requirement allows two behaviours a user would notice, choose the more conservative one, record it as "pending review", and continue.

Also non-blocking, record and continue: a finding listed in project/00_setup/pre-approved.md whose evidence matches (cite its ID, apply its action, do not ask); a pinned tool that runs but reports another version; a scanner analyser disabled for lack of credentials; dev-only tooling added under the `tech-stack.md` rule.

## Decision record

Append each decision to `docs/decisions-log.md` in this format:

```
## D-nn: <short title>
- Timestamp:
- Phase:
- Type: blocking | non-blocking
- Trigger: <what happened; cite IDs and files>
- Options: <numbered alternatives; mark the proposed default>
- Human response: <answer and time, or "none">
- Resolution: <chosen option> | pending review
```

- Never delete or rewrite a record; add a follow-up record instead.
- The phase 7 gate fails while any record lacks a resolution.

## Identifiers

| Prefix | Meaning | Defined in |
|---|---|---|
| `US-nnn` / `AC-nnn-nn` | User story / acceptance criterion | `project/01_requirements/user-stories.md` / `project/01_requirements/acceptance-criteria.md` |
| `BR-nn` / `OQ-nn` | Business rule / open question | `project/01_requirements/` |
| `AR-nn` | Architecture constraint | `project/02_design/architecture.md` |
| `SB-nn` / `SR-nn` | Security baseline / project security requirement | `general/security/` / `project/02_design/security-requirements.md` |
| `ES-nn` | Engineering standard | `general/engineering-standards.md` |
| `NFR-nn` | Non-functional requirement | `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md` |
| `DoD-nn` / `DoD-Pnn` | Done criterion, general / project | `general/quality/` / `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md` |
| `F-nn` / `D-nn` | Finding / decision | `docs/06_verification-report.md` / `docs/decisions-log.md` |

Tests, commits and findings reference these IDs.

## Commits

Commit as a human developer would: small, finished steps, never half a project. The report measures every point below on every commit, so each is a check, not advice.

- One commit = one logical change that can be reverted alone. Commit it when its checks pass, **before** starting the next change. Never collect several changes in the working tree and split them afterwards with commits in a row (commits less than 60 seconds apart are counted as a burst).
- Size: at most 15 files and 400 changed lines, not counting logs, lock files and generated files. Check with `git diff --cached --shortstat` before every commit and split when over, for example by layer (domain and use case, then persistence and adapters, then web/API, then UI), or by test class group. "State why it cannot be split" is only for a single generated file.
- One category per commit: code, tests, documents, or build/dependency files. Never mix them, and never add a document change (decision log, progress, README) to a code, test or build commit. A component skeleton is two commits: the build file with its pinned dependencies (`build`), then the source files (`chore`). A test harness or a docker/compose file is its own commit.
- Each fix (`F-nn`) is its own commit.
- The build passes at every commit and no previously passing test fails. Frozen acceptance and end-to-end tests of behaviour not yet built may fail.
- Message: `<type>: <summary> (IDs)`; type `feat`, `test`, `fix`, `refactor`, `docs`, `build` or `chore`; imperative; the **whole subject line including the IDs is at most 72 characters**. Name at most three IDs or one range (`AC-003-01..03`) in the subject; put the rest in the message body. Example: `feat: store registrations in one transaction (US-001, AC-001-01..07)`.
- Units per phase: `general/phases.md`. Working tree clean at every gate, apart from `03_statistics/` (the clock tool changes `run-log.json` all the time; do not commit it phase by phase).
- Do not squash, rebase or rewrite history.

## Progress

Update `docs/00_progress.md` at every gate and before any stop, so a fresh session can resume.

## Output

- Write command output longer than 50 lines to `out/logs/`; report only a summary and the path.
- Use only the severity levels in `general/quality/severity-scale.md`.

## Secrets (`.env`)

You never need to see a secret value; the tools that run need it, not you.

- Do not read `.env` with a file tool, and do not print, copy or log its values: no `cat`, `echo`, `env`, `printenv` or `docker compose config` on it, in commands, files, logs, commit messages or the conversation.
- Pass values to tools without showing them: `docker compose --env-file .env`, or `export NAME="$(sed -n 's/^NAME=//p' .env | tr -d '\r')"` inside the command that needs it.
- Check presence and emptiness only, as in `general/skills/preflight`.
- Before saving output from a command that may print an environment, filter it so no value is written.
- The phase 6 secret-leak check (`general/skills/verify-release`) must find nothing.

## Statistics

Record with `03_statistics/tools/stat.mjs`, which writes the real clock: `init` once in phase 0; `phase <n> start` and `phase <n> end` at every phase boundary (a start closes the previous phase, `phase 7 end` closes the run); `wait start <cause> "<reason>" [decisionId]` and `wait end` around every wait for the human, including stops and restarts. Edit `03_statistics/run-log.json` directly for test runs, findings, fix loops, decisions, deviations and quality results, as defined in `03_statistics/metrics.md`, and write `03_statistics/run-summary.md` in phase 7. Do nothing else in `03_statistics/`; in particular do not run `tools/build-report.mjs`, which belongs to the post-run session.
----
# Progress

> Written in: every phase · Agent: writes

Updated at every gate and before any stop, so a fresh session can resume from here.

- Workflow:
- Current phase:
- Last gate result:
- Next step:
- Waiting for the human on: <decision ids, or "nothing">

- The phase 3 commits add no production code beyond the bootstrap skeleton; the freeze commit adds the manifest, and every file it lists was committed earlier in phase 3.
- Build has at least one commit per user story, each naming its `US`/`AC` ID; no commit exceeds 15 files or 400 lines or mixes code, tests, documents and build files (`working-rules.md`, Commits). The report measures message length, bursts and size on every commit, so the agent does not audit commit subjects itself.
- Every hash in the manifest still matches.
----
# Working rules

> Owner: Team lead · Read in: every phase · Agent: read-only

## Ask the human (blocking)

Record a decision in `docs/decisions-log.md` (format under "Decision record"), ask, and wait when:

- anything checked in phase 0 is missing or wrong and only a human can fix it;
- a technology, version or service from `project/00_setup/tech-stack.md` does not work or needs changing;
- a frozen acceptance test appears wrong (only a human may update the manifest afterwards);
- a Critical or High finding would be downgraded or accepted.

Ask all open questions of a phase in one message. While waiting, finish work that does not depend on the answer.

## Decide and record (non-blocking)

When a requirement allows two behaviours a user would notice, choose the more conservative one, record it as "pending review", and continue.

Also non-blocking, record and continue: a finding listed in project/00_setup/pre-approved.md whose evidence matches (cite its ID, apply its action, do not ask); a pinned tool that runs but reports another version; a scanner analyser disabled for lack of credentials; dev-only tooling added under the `tech-stack.md` rule.

## Decision record

Append each decision to `docs/decisions-log.md` in this format:

```
## D-nn: <short title>
- Timestamp:
- Phase:
- Type: blocking | non-blocking
- Trigger: <what happened; cite IDs and files>
- Options: <numbered alternatives; mark the proposed default>
- Human response: <answer and time, or "none">
- Resolution: <chosen option> | pending review
```

- Never delete or rewrite a record; add a follow-up record instead.
- The phase 7 gate fails while any record lacks a resolution.

## Identifiers

| Prefix | Meaning | Defined in |
|---|---|---|
| `US-nnn` / `AC-nnn-nn` | User story / acceptance criterion | `project/01_requirements/user-stories.md` / `project/01_requirements/acceptance-criteria.md` |
| `BR-nn` / `OQ-nn` | Business rule / open question | `project/01_requirements/` |
| `AR-nn` | Architecture constraint | `project/02_design/architecture.md` |
| `SB-nn` / `SR-nn` | Security baseline / project security requirement | `general/security/` / `project/02_design/security-requirements.md` |
| `ES-nn` | Engineering standard | `general/engineering-standards.md` |
| `NFR-nn` | Non-functional requirement | `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md` |
| `DoD-nn` / `DoD-Pnn` | Done criterion, general / project | `general/quality/` / `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md` |
| `F-nn` / `D-nn` | Finding / decision | `docs/06_verification-report.md` / `docs/decisions-log.md` |

Tests, commits and findings reference these IDs.

## Commits

Commit as a human developer would: small, finished steps, never half a project. The report measures every point below on every commit, so each is a check, not advice.

- One commit = one logical change that can be reverted alone. Commit it when its checks pass, **before** starting the next change. Never collect several changes in the working tree and split them afterwards with commits in a row (commits less than 60 seconds apart are counted as a burst).
- Size: at most 15 files and 400 changed lines, not counting logs, lock files and generated files. Check with `git diff --cached --shortstat` before every commit and split when over, for example by layer (domain and use case, then persistence and adapters, then web/API, then UI), or by test class group. "State why it cannot be split" is only for a single generated file.
- One category per commit: code, tests, documents, or build/dependency files. Never mix them, and never add a document change (decision log, progress, README) to a code, test or build commit. A component skeleton is two commits: the build file with its pinned dependencies (`build`), then the source files (`chore`). A test harness or a docker/compose file is its own commit.
- Each fix (`F-nn`) is its own commit.
- The build passes at every commit and no previously passing test fails. Frozen acceptance and end-to-end tests of behaviour not yet built may fail.
- Message: `<type>: <summary> (IDs)`; type `feat`, `test`, `fix`, `refactor`, `docs`, `build` or `chore`; imperative; the **whole subject line including the IDs is at most 72 characters**. Name at most three IDs or one range (`AC-003-01..03`) in the subject; put the rest in the message body. Example: `feat: store registrations in one transaction (US-001, AC-001-01..07)`.
- Units per phase: `general/phases.md`. Working tree clean at every gate, apart from `03_statistics/` (the clock tool changes `run-log.json` all the time; do not commit it phase by phase).
- Do not squash, rebase or rewrite history.

## Progress

Update `docs/00_progress.md` at every gate and before any stop, so a fresh session can resume.

## Output

- Write command output longer than 50 lines to `out/logs/`; report only a summary and the path.
- Use only the severity levels in `general/quality/severity-scale.md`.

## Secrets (`.env`)

You never need to see a secret value; the tools that run need it, not you.

- Do not read `.env` with a file tool, and do not print, copy or log its values: no `cat`, `echo`, `env`, `printenv` or `docker compose config` on it, in commands, files, logs, commit messages or the conversation.
- Pass values to tools without showing them: `docker compose --env-file .env`, or `export NAME="$(sed -n 's/^NAME=//p' .env | tr -d '\r')"` inside the command that needs it.
- Check presence and emptiness only, as in `general/skills/preflight`.
- Before saving output from a command that may print an environment, filter it so no value is written.
- The phase 6 secret-leak check (`general/skills/verify-release`) must find nothing.

## Statistics

Record with `03_statistics/tools/stat.mjs`, which writes the real clock: `init` once in phase 0; `phase <n> start` and `phase <n> end` at every phase boundary (a start closes the previous phase, `phase 7 end` closes the run); `wait start <cause> "<reason>" [decisionId]` and `wait end` around every wait for the human, including stops and restarts. Edit `03_statistics/run-log.json` directly for test runs, findings, fix loops, decisions, deviations and quality results, as defined in `03_statistics/metrics.md`, and write `03_statistics/run-summary.md` in phase 7. Do nothing else in `03_statistics/`; in particular do not run `tools/build-report.mjs`, which belongs to the post-run session.
----
# Progress

> Written in: every phase · Agent: writes

Updated at every gate and before any stop, so a fresh session can resume from here.

- Workflow:
- Current phase:
- Last gate result:
- Next step:
- Waiting for the human on: <decision ids, or "nothing">

# Security baseline

> Owner: Security officer · Read in: phases 0, 2, 6 · Agent: read-only

Applies to every project. Project requirements (`SR-nn`) and the chosen standard level are in `project/02_design/security-requirements.md`.

## Verification standard by component type

| Component type | Standard | Default level |
|---|---|---|
| Web app, API, service | OWASP ASVS (latest) | Level 1; Level 2 when handling authentication, payments or sensitive personal data |
| Mobile app | OWASP MASVS (latest) | L1 |
| Desktop app, CLI, library | Applicable OWASP ASVS chapters | Level 1 |

## Controls for every project

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SB-01 | All input is validated on the trusted side (server or core), whatever the client does. |
| SB-02 | Every non-public operation checks authentication and authorization. |
| SB-03 | Credentials are stored only as salted, slow hashes; secrets come from configuration (ES-01, ES-02). |
| SB-04 | Data in transit uses TLS outside the local machine. |
| SB-05 | Output is encoded for its context; queries are parameterised. |
| SB-06 | Public and authentication endpoints are rate limited. |
| SB-07 | Errors and logs expose no internals, secrets or personal data (ES-07). |
| SB-08 | Dependencies are scanned; no known Critical or High vulnerability ships. |
| SB-09 | Source is scanned with static analysis and a secret scanner. |
| SB-10 | Web responses carry security headers (content security policy, framing, content-type options). |
| SB-11 | Deployed processes run with least privilege (e.g. non-root containers). |

## Personal data (privacy)

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SB-12 | Collect only the personal data a requirement needs; the project lists it. |
| SB-13 | Each personal-data item has a stated purpose and retention period. |
| SB-14 | Consent, where required, is explicit and never preselected. |

# Severity scale

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phases 0, 6, 7 · Agent: read-only

The only levels used anywhere. Critical and High block release.

| Level | Definition | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Critical | Exploitable now, or total loss of a core user story with no workaround | Unauthenticated access to protected data; accepted input that is silently not stored |
| High | Exploitable under realistic conditions, or a core user story degraded for a plausible group of users | Missing authorization check on one operation; a limit that locks out legitimate users |
| Medium | A real defect with limited impact, or a control weaker than required | A dependency vulnerability with no reachable exploit path; a duplicated validation rule |
| Low | Cosmetic, stylistic, or a theoretical or false-positive finding | A lint warning; a scanner match on constant input |

## Rules

- Tools that report Critical/High/Medium/Low (or CVSS) are used as reported.
- Lowering a Critical or High to Medium or Low needs written evidence (e.g. the vulnerable feature is not used) and is a blocking decision.
- A surviving mutant in security-, validation- or persistence-related code is classified individually.

## Tool mapping

Extend when a project adds a tool with its own scale.

| Tool type | Tool's level | Maps to |
|---|---|---|
| CVSS-based (dependency scanners) | 9.0–10.0 / 7.0–8.9 / 4.0–6.9 / 0.1–3.9 | Critical / High / Medium / Low |
| Rule-based SAST with ERROR/WARNING/INFO | ERROR / WARNING / INFO | High / Medium / Low |
| Rank or priority 1–5 scales | 1 / 2 / 3–5 | High / Medium / Low |
| Bug-rank 1–20 scales | 1–4 / 5–9 / 10–20 | High / Medium / Low |
==== 03_statistics/metrics.md
# Metrics

> Owner: Experiment lead · Read in: every phase and post-run · Agent: read-only

Experiment measurement only. Record observed values; never estimate. An unobservable value stays `null` with a `<field>Reason`.

Goal column: **↓** lower is better, **↑** higher is better, **=** should equal the stated value, **i** information for interpreting other numbers.

## Principles

- **Human waiting is not part of the result.** Agent time is wall time minus every wait for a human. A wait over one hour also lets the 1-hour prompt cache expire, and the call after it writes the whole context again; that rebuild is a cost of the wait, so `usage.costUsdExclWaits` removes it. Compare runs on agent time and `costUsdExclWaits`.
- **Record only what only you can see, and with the clock tool.** The agent records what happened (waits, loops, decisions, deviations, test and quality results). Timestamps come from `tools/stat.mjs`, never from memory or estimates. Everything that can be computed from the transcripts and git is computed after the run by `tools/build-report.mjs`, so the run spends no calls on it.
- **Make runs comparable.** Say what a number covers. Scope, level and tool of coverage, mutation score and code size are defined in `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`.

## 1. Agent, during the run → `run-log.json`

Phase 0, first action: `node 03_statistics/tools/stat.mjs init`. It creates `run-log.json` from the template, a unique `runId`, the start time and commit, the transcript path and the environment. It prints what it wrote.

| Field | When | How | Goal |
|---|---|---|---|
| `runId`, `model`, `effort`, `templateVersion`, `start`, `startCommit`, `transcript`, `environment` | phase 0 | written by `stat.mjs init` from `run-config.md`, git and the host | i |
| `phases[].start`, `phases[].end` | every phase boundary | `stat.mjs phase <n> start` and `stat.mjs phase <n> end`; a start also closes the previous phase, `phase 7 end` also sets `end` and `finalCommit` | ↓ agent time per phase |
| `humanInterventions[]` | every time the agent waits for the human or the human acts, including stops, restarts and installs | `stat.mjs wait start <cause> "<reason>" [decisionId]` when you ask or stop, `stat.mjs wait end` when work resumes. `cause`: `decision`, `environment`, `approval`, `session`, `other` | ↓ count and minutes; every minute here is excluded from agent time |
| `firstTestRun`, `finalTestRun` | first full run before fixes; last full run | edit the file: `passed`, `failed` and `byLevel` (`unit`, `integration`, `acceptance`, `architecture`, `e2e` counts) | first: ↓ failed (defects the first run found); final: ↑ passed, `failed` = 0 |
| `acceptanceCriteria` | end of phase 3; changes in phase 4 | `total` criteria, `frozenTests`, `frozenTestChanges[]` as `{decisionId, reason}` | ↑ criteria covered by tests; ↓ frozen-test changes (each one needed a human) |
| `findings` | end of phase 6 | counts by severity, as found | ↓ |
| `openAtEnd` | end of phase 6 | Critical, High and Medium findings still open after triage | = 0 for Critical and High |
| `fixLoops[]` | each verify → fix → re-verify loop | `{loop, findings, category, needsHuman, change, start, end}`. `category`: `test-gap`, `security-config`, `dependency`, `defect`, `process`, `tooling`. `start` is the first fix action, `end` the clean re-check (UTC, `date -u +%FT%TZ`) | ↓ minutes per loop; a loop that repeats across runs belongs in the template |
| `decisions[]` | each decision record | `{id, type, phase, category, start, end}`; `type` `blocking` or `non-blocking`; `category`: `environment`, `dependency`, `security-finding`, `frozen-test`, `requirement`, `other`; `end` = when resolved | ↓ blocking; a category that repeats across runs can be answered in advance |
| `divergences[]` | whenever the run departs from `AGENTS.md`, `working-rules.md`, `phases.md` or the stack | `{phase, ref, divergence}`; includes steps done without the required question, scope reduced, versions replaced | = 0; each one makes the run less comparable |
| `codeMetrics` | phase 5, updated in phase 6 for a changed component | per component: `productionLoc`, `testLoc`, `lineCoverage` and `branchCoverage` as `{unit, nonUnit, all}`, `mutation` as `{score, scoreAdjusted, scoreCovered, killed, equivalent, total, covered, scope, tests, tool, excluded}`, plus complexity and duplication; scope, level and counting as in `general/quality/measurement-scope.md` | ↑ coverage and mutation score (always with scope); = 0 duplication |
| `codeMetrics.gate` | phase 5, updated in phase 6 | the quality gate of `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`: `thresholds`, `perComponent` (`lineMet`, `mutationMet`, shortfalls in points), `mutationRounds` and `testsAtFirstMutation` per component, `met` | `met` true; few rounds |

`commits[]` and `commitSummary` are not recorded by the agent: the post-run step reads them from `git log`.

## 2. Post-run session → `run-log.json`, `results/`, `data/`

Started automatically by the Stop and SessionEnd hooks in `.claude/settings.json` once `run-log.json` has an `end`; if the hooks did not run, in a new session whose only task is: "Run `node 03_statistics/tools/build-report.mjs --run 03_statistics` and report what it prints. Do not change anything else." Nothing is typed in by hand. The script:

1. measures the run from the session transcript(s), the sub-agent transcripts next to them and `git log`, and stores `time`, `usage`, `environment`, `commits`, `commitSummary` in `run-log.json`;
2. copies the transcripts to `03_statistics/data/` (committed with the run, so the measuring can be repeated on any machine; the recorded path is used when it exists, the copy otherwise);
3. writes everything it generates to `03_statistics/results/`: `run-report.html` (every attribute with goal, direction and value), `measurements.json`, `usage-summary.md`, `commits.csv`, `transcript.md` (readable session, needs Python 3);

Options: `--no-write` leaves `run-log.json` and `usage.md` alone, `--no-md` skips `transcript.md`, `--no-backup` skips `data/`. If `transcript` is missing from `run-log.json`, find the session with `py 03_statistics/tools/claude_chat_to_md.py --list`, put the path of its `.jsonl` in `transcript` (a resumed run lists every session file in `transcripts`) and run the script again. Without any transcript the report still builds from phases and recorded waits; cost, tokens, model and tool time, context and cache rebuilds are then not recorded.

| Field | What it is | Goal |
|---|---|---|
| `time.agentMin` | sum over phases of wall time minus waits (recorded interventions and idle gaps above 10 minutes in the transcript) | ↓ |
| `time.humanWaitMin`, `time.waitsOver60Min`, `time.longWaits[]` | excluded waiting, and each wait over an hour with its cause | ↓; = 0 waits over an hour |
| `time.modelMin`, `time.toolMin` | transcript time spent generating and running tools | ↓; tool time shows what to automate or speed up |
| `time.unrecordedIdleMin` | idle time in the transcript that `humanInterventions` does not cover | = 0 (a recording gap) |
| `time.phaseChecks` | phase boundaries written by `stat.mjs` against typed ones, and implausible timestamps | all via `stat.mjs`, no issues |
| `time.byPhase[]` | wall, wait, agent, model and tool minutes per phase | ↓ in phases 0, 1, 2, 7 (overhead); phases 4 to 6 hold the real work |
| `usage.inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `thinkingTokens`, `cacheReadTokens`, `cacheWriteTokens`, `modelCalls` | sums over every model call, each call counted once, sub-agents included | ↓ |
| `usage.toolCalls` | total, errors, per tool name | ↓ calls and errors |
| `usage.costUsd` | tokens × the prices in `usage.md`, per model | ↓ |
| `usage.costUsdExclWaits` | `costUsd` minus the cache rebuilds that followed a wait over an hour | ↓ (the comparison figure) |
| `usage.cacheRebuilds[]` | each cache write above 150k tokens, the wait before it and its extra cost | = none caused by waits |
| `usage.subagents` | sub-agent calls, transcripts found, their cost (inside `costUsd`) | i; a call without a transcript is a measuring gap |
| `usage.byPhase[]` | calls, tokens, cost and average context per phase | ↓ in late phases, where context is largest |
| `usage.context` | peak and average context tokens per call, share of calls above 150k | ↓ (every call re-reads the whole context) |
| `usage.toolTimeByCategory` | minutes and calls per command class (backend build, mutation, e2e, …) | ↓ for the largest classes |
| `commits[]` | per commit: phase, type, files, changed lines (without logs, lock files, generated folders), concerns touched, size and message checks, minutes since the previous commit (waits removed), model calls and cost since the previous commit | commits small and finished: ≤ 15 files and ≤ 400 lines, one concern, `<type>: <summary> (IDs)` |
| `commitSummary` | counts, median and maximum size, shares over the size guide, mixed, with a correct message, in a burst (within a minute of the previous), cost and minutes between commits, cost per 100 lines | ↓ oversize, mixed and burst; ↑ correct messages |
| `environment` | operator, machine, plan, permission mode (from `run-config.md`), the host the run started on (account, CPU, memory, working directory; read by `stat.mjs init`), operating system and tool versions (at the start), harness version, entry point, models, effort and permission modes seen (from the transcripts), measuring host | i; needed to explain differences between runs |

## 3. Human → `usage.md`

Prices before the post-run session (one row per model id, shape as in the file). After it only `Approval prompts` is yours; the other cells are filled automatically when empty, and anything you wrote stays. A mismatch between the harness's total and our calculation is reported in the last row.

==== Run_Guide.md
# Run guide

> Feature experiment (template 1.7-ft): the folder name and branch follow `<user>/single-agent/sdd/v001/run-<n>[-<feature>]`, and greenfield and brownfield runs have extra steps. Follow `instructions/normal.md`, `greenfield.md` or `brownfield.md` on the `experiment` branch; they list only what differs from this guide. Clone with `--single-branch -b main` so the `experiment` branch never reaches the run folder.

This setup is run three times, once each by kyuhi, tanej and tjan, in one shared environment, and the three runs are compared. Everything below is therefore the same for everyone; the only things that may differ are the four lines in the table "If you are not kyuhi".

## 1. Prepare the run folder (clone, branch, .env)
1. **Clone the template** into a new folder named after the run (`kyuhi_single-agent_sdd_v007`). Branch `main` is the template you clone and never commit to it.
   ```bash
   git clone --single-branch -b main https://github.com/SQA-interns/feature-testing.git <user>_single-agent_sdd_<version>
   cd <user>_single-agent_sdd_<version>
   ```
   
2. **Create the run's branch** (it is the only branch you work and push on): `<user>/single-agent/sdd/<version>`, for kyuhi `kyuhi/single-agent/sdd/v007`:
   ```bash
   git switch -c <user>/single-agent/sdd/<version>
   ```
   
3. **Keep `.env` out of git before you create it** (the template has no `.gitignore`; the agent writes one in phase 0):
   - Git Bash: `echo .env >> .git/info/exclude`
   - PowerShell: `Add-Content -Encoding ascii .git\info\exclude ".env"`
     
4. **Check and update values in `01_input/01_project/00_setup/run-config.md`** (change the values to match your environment).
      - operator `kyuhi`,
      - machine `kyuhiPC`,
      - plan `PRO`,
      - permission mode `auto`,
      - model `claude-opus-5-5`,
      - effort `medium`
      - Run label: **change it for every run** (`kyuhi_single-agent_sdd_v001`, then `v002`,...).
      - Run ID: **keep empty it generates by itself**
      - Starting commit: **keep empty it generates by itself**
        
5. **Check the price row in `03_statistics/usage.md`.** It is pre-filled for Opus 5.5; change it only if the prices or the model changed.

6. **Create `.env`**: copy `01_input/01_project/00_setup/secrets.env.example` to `.env` in the run folder and fill every value (database password, organizer login, NVD key). Never paste a secret into the chat.

7. **Commit your changes to `run-config.md` (and `usage.md`, if you changed it)** so the starting commit contains the right user, machine, plan and label: `git add -A`, `git commit -m "run setup <run label>"`. If you changed nothing there is nothing to commit and the starting commit is the commit of `main` you cloned. Check that `git status` does not list `.env` before anything is pushed.

8. **Push the run's branch** (so the start state is on record before the agent starts; `origin` is already set by the clone):
   ```bash
   git push -u origin <user>/single-agent/sdd/<version>
   ```
   Use your own config in the branch. Every user pushes to a branch of its own, never to `main`. Do not push before `.env` is confirmed absent from `git status`.
   
9. **Set the same permission mode** you set in `run-config.md`.
10. **Check the environment** (the same for all three operators): Docker Engine 29.8.1 and Compose 5.5.1, Node 24.13.0, Java 21, internet access for the scanners (NVD key in `.env`), no other heavy load on the machine during the run, one session only.

# Severity scale

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phases 0, 6, 7 · Agent: read-only

The only levels used anywhere. Critical and High block release.

| Level | Definition | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Critical | Exploitable now, or total loss of a core user story with no workaround | Unauthenticated access to protected data; accepted input that is silently not stored |
| High | Exploitable under realistic conditions, or a core user story degraded for a plausible group of users | Missing authorization check on one operation; a limit that locks out legitimate users |
| Medium | A real defect with limited impact, or a control weaker than required | A dependency vulnerability with no reachable exploit path; a duplicated validation rule |
| Low | Cosmetic, stylistic, or a theoretical or false-positive finding | A lint warning; a scanner match on constant input |

## Rules

- Tools that report Critical/High/Medium/Low (or CVSS) are used as reported.
- Lowering a Critical or High to Medium or Low needs written evidence (e.g. the vulnerable feature is not used) and is a blocking decision.
- A surviving mutant in security-, validation- or persistence-related code is classified individually.

## Tool mapping

Extend when a project adds a tool with its own scale.

| Tool type | Tool's level | Maps to |
|---|---|---|
| CVSS-based (dependency scanners) | 9.0–10.0 / 7.0–8.9 / 4.0–6.9 / 0.1–3.9 | Critical / High / Medium / Low |
| Rule-based SAST with ERROR/WARNING/INFO | ERROR / WARNING / INFO | High / Medium / Low |
| Rank or priority 1–5 scales | 1 / 2 / 3–5 | High / Medium / Low |
| Bug-rank 1–20 scales | 1–4 / 5–9 / 10–20 | High / Medium / Low |
==== 03_statistics/metrics.md
# Metrics

> Owner: Experiment lead · Read in: every phase and post-run · Agent: read-only

Experiment measurement only. Record observed values; never estimate. An unobservable value stays `null` with a `<field>Reason`.

Goal column: **↓** lower is better, **↑** higher is better, **=** should equal the stated value, **i** information for interpreting other numbers.

## Principles

- **Human waiting is not part of the result.** Agent time is wall time minus every wait for a human. A wait over one hour also lets the 1-hour prompt cache expire, and the call after it writes the whole context again; that rebuild is a cost of the wait, so `usage.costUsdExclWaits` removes it. Compare runs on agent time and `costUsdExclWaits`.
- **Record only what only you can see, and with the clock tool.** The agent records what happened (waits, loops, decisions, deviations, test and quality results). Timestamps come from `tools/stat.mjs`, never from memory or estimates. Everything that can be computed from the transcripts and git is computed after the run by `tools/build-report.mjs`, so the run spends no calls on it.
- **Make runs comparable.** Say what a number covers. Scope, level and tool of coverage, mutation score and code size are defined in `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`.

## 1. Agent, during the run → `run-log.json`

Phase 0, first action: `node 03_statistics/tools/stat.mjs init`. It creates `run-log.json` from the template, a unique `runId`, the start time and commit, the transcript path and the environment. It prints what it wrote.

| Field | When | How | Goal |
|---|---|---|---|
| `runId`, `model`, `effort`, `templateVersion`, `start`, `startCommit`, `transcript`, `environment` | phase 0 | written by `stat.mjs init` from `run-config.md`, git and the host | i |
| `phases[].start`, `phases[].end` | every phase boundary | `stat.mjs phase <n> start` and `stat.mjs phase <n> end`; a start also closes the previous phase, `phase 7 end` also sets `end` and `finalCommit` | ↓ agent time per phase |
| `humanInterventions[]` | every time the agent waits for the human or the human acts, including stops, restarts and installs | `stat.mjs wait start <cause> "<reason>" [decisionId]` when you ask or stop, `stat.mjs wait end` when work resumes. `cause`: `decision`, `environment`, `approval`, `session`, `other` | ↓ count and minutes; every minute here is excluded from agent time |
| `firstTestRun`, `finalTestRun` | first full run before fixes; last full run | edit the file: `passed`, `failed` and `byLevel` (`unit`, `integration`, `acceptance`, `architecture`, `e2e` counts) | first: ↓ failed (defects the first run found); final: ↑ passed, `failed` = 0 |
| `acceptanceCriteria` | end of phase 3; changes in phase 4 | `total` criteria, `frozenTests`, `frozenTestChanges[]` as `{decisionId, reason}` | ↑ criteria covered by tests; ↓ frozen-test changes (each one needed a human) |
| `findings` | end of phase 6 | counts by severity, as found | ↓ |
| `openAtEnd` | end of phase 6 | Critical, High and Medium findings still open after triage | = 0 for Critical and High |
| `fixLoops[]` | each verify → fix → re-verify loop | `{loop, findings, category, needsHuman, change, start, end}`. `category`: `test-gap`, `security-config`, `dependency`, `defect`, `process`, `tooling`. `start` is the first fix action, `end` the clean re-check (UTC, `date -u +%FT%TZ`) | ↓ minutes per loop; a loop that repeats across runs belongs in the template |
| `decisions[]` | each decision record | `{id, type, phase, category, start, end}`; `type` `blocking` or `non-blocking`; `category`: `environment`, `dependency`, `security-finding`, `frozen-test`, `requirement`, `other`; `end` = when resolved | ↓ blocking; a category that repeats across runs can be answered in advance |
| `divergences[]` | whenever the run departs from `AGENTS.md`, `working-rules.md`, `phases.md` or the stack | `{phase, ref, divergence}`; includes steps done without the required question, scope reduced, versions replaced | = 0; each one makes the run less comparable |
| `codeMetrics` | phase 5, updated in phase 6 for a changed component | per component: `productionLoc`, `testLoc`, `lineCoverage` and `branchCoverage` as `{unit, nonUnit, all}`, `mutation` as `{score, scoreAdjusted, scoreCovered, killed, equivalent, total, covered, scope, tests, tool, excluded}`, plus complexity and duplication; scope, level and counting as in `general/quality/measurement-scope.md` | ↑ coverage and mutation score (always with scope); = 0 duplication |
| `codeMetrics.gate` | phase 5, updated in phase 6 | the quality gate of `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`: `thresholds`, `perComponent` (`lineMet`, `mutationMet`, shortfalls in points), `mutationRounds` and `testsAtFirstMutation` per component, `met` | `met` true; few rounds |

`commits[]` and `commitSummary` are not recorded by the agent: the post-run step reads them from `git log`.

## 2. Post-run session → `run-log.json`, `results/`, `data/`

Started automatically by the Stop and SessionEnd hooks in `.claude/settings.json` once `run-log.json` has an `end`; if the hooks did not run, in a new session whose only task is: "Run `node 03_statistics/tools/build-report.mjs --run 03_statistics` and report what it prints. Do not change anything else." Nothing is typed in by hand. The script:

1. measures the run from the session transcript(s), the sub-agent transcripts next to them and `git log`, and stores `time`, `usage`, `environment`, `commits`, `commitSummary` in `run-log.json`;
2. copies the transcripts to `03_statistics/data/` (committed with the run, so the measuring can be repeated on any machine; the recorded path is used when it exists, the copy otherwise);
3. writes everything it generates to `03_statistics/results/`: `run-report.html` (every attribute with goal, direction and value), `measurements.json`, `usage-summary.md`, `commits.csv`, `transcript.md` (readable session, needs Python 3);

Options: `--no-write` leaves `run-log.json` and `usage.md` alone, `--no-md` skips `transcript.md`, `--no-backup` skips `data/`. If `transcript` is missing from `run-log.json`, find the session with `py 03_statistics/tools/claude_chat_to_md.py --list`, put the path of its `.jsonl` in `transcript` (a resumed run lists every session file in `transcripts`) and run the script again. Without any transcript the report still builds from phases and recorded waits; cost, tokens, model and tool time, context and cache rebuilds are then not recorded.

| Field | What it is | Goal |
|---|---|---|
| `time.agentMin` | sum over phases of wall time minus waits (recorded interventions and idle gaps above 10 minutes in the transcript) | ↓ |
| `time.humanWaitMin`, `time.waitsOver60Min`, `time.longWaits[]` | excluded waiting, and each wait over an hour with its cause | ↓; = 0 waits over an hour |
| `time.modelMin`, `time.toolMin` | transcript time spent generating and running tools | ↓; tool time shows what to automate or speed up |
| `time.unrecordedIdleMin` | idle time in the transcript that `humanInterventions` does not cover | = 0 (a recording gap) |
| `time.phaseChecks` | phase boundaries written by `stat.mjs` against typed ones, and implausible timestamps | all via `stat.mjs`, no issues |
| `time.byPhase[]` | wall, wait, agent, model and tool minutes per phase | ↓ in phases 0, 1, 2, 7 (overhead); phases 4 to 6 hold the real work |
| `usage.inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `thinkingTokens`, `cacheReadTokens`, `cacheWriteTokens`, `modelCalls` | sums over every model call, each call counted once, sub-agents included | ↓ |
| `usage.toolCalls` | total, errors, per tool name | ↓ calls and errors |
| `usage.costUsd` | tokens × the prices in `usage.md`, per model | ↓ |
| `usage.costUsdExclWaits` | `costUsd` minus the cache rebuilds that followed a wait over an hour | ↓ (the comparison figure) |
| `usage.cacheRebuilds[]` | each cache write above 150k tokens, the wait before it and its extra cost | = none caused by waits |
| `usage.subagents` | sub-agent calls, transcripts found, their cost (inside `costUsd`) | i; a call without a transcript is a measuring gap |
| `usage.byPhase[]` | calls, tokens, cost and average context per phase | ↓ in late phases, where context is largest |
| `usage.context` | peak and average context tokens per call, share of calls above 150k | ↓ (every call re-reads the whole context) |
| `usage.toolTimeByCategory` | minutes and calls per command class (backend build, mutation, e2e, …) | ↓ for the largest classes |
| `commits[]` | per commit: phase, type, files, changed lines (without logs, lock files, generated folders), concerns touched, size and message checks, minutes since the previous commit (waits removed), model calls and cost since the previous commit | commits small and finished: ≤ 15 files and ≤ 400 lines, one concern, `<type>: <summary> (IDs)` |
| `commitSummary` | counts, median and maximum size, shares over the size guide, mixed, with a correct message, in a burst (within a minute of the previous), cost and minutes between commits, cost per 100 lines | ↓ oversize, mixed and burst; ↑ correct messages |
| `environment` | operator, machine, plan, permission mode (from `run-config.md`), the host the run started on (account, CPU, memory, working directory; read by `stat.mjs init`), operating system and tool versions (at the start), harness version, entry point, models, effort and permission modes seen (from the transcripts), measuring host | i; needed to explain differences between runs |

## 3. Human → `usage.md`

Prices before the post-run session (one row per model id, shape as in the file). After it only `Approval prompts` is yours; the other cells are filled automatically when empty, and anything you wrote stays. A mismatch between the harness's total and our calculation is reported in the last row.

content.content:
# Architecture

> Owner: Architect · Read in: phases 0, 2, 4, 6, 7 · Agent: read-only

## Components

Each component gets its own folder and README in `02_output/`. Versions come only from `tech-stack.md`; reference its ids, never repeat a version here.

```yaml
components:
  - name: backend
    type: api
    folder: 02_output/backend
    platform: java
    build: maven-wrapper
    bootstrap: Maven wrapper plus a hand-written pom.xml whose parent is org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-parent; root package si.konferenca.registration
    commands:          # ES-05; filled in phase 0 if left empty
      build:
      test:
      check:
      run:
    depends_on: []
    deploys_as: container image (eclipse-temurin base, non-root)
  - name: frontend
    type: web-app
    folder: 02_output/frontend
    platform: node
    build: vite
    bootstrap: hand-written package.json with the exact tech-stack.md versions and a committed package-lock.json (no project generator)
    commands:
      build:
      test:
      check:
      run:
    depends_on: [backend]
    deploys_as: container image (static files served by nginx)
```

The local stack (both components, PostgreSQL, mail catcher) is started with `02_output/docker-compose.yml`.

## Constraints

Checkable rules the code must respect (layering, allowed dependencies, patterns). Checked automatically in phase 6 where the stack allows (DoD-04).

| ID | Constraint |
|---|---|
| AR-01 | The frontend talks to the backend only through the REST API under `/api`. |
| AR-02 | The backend's internal architecture is not prescribed: the agent declares and justifies it in `docs/02_specification.md` and then writes ArchUnit rules that check exactly that declaration. |
| AR-03 | No package cycles in the backend (ArchUnit slice check). |
| AR-04 | Conference options change through configuration only, without code changes and without changing the fixed participant fields (BR-01). The mechanism is decided in phase 2. |
| AR-05 | A success response is sent only after both the database row and the JSON copy are written (BR-06, BR-07). |
| AR-06 | The database schema changes only through Flyway migrations (ES-08). |
| AR-07 | The frontend contains no secret; the reCAPTCHA site key is its only key and comes from configuration. |
| AR-09 | The REST API under `/api` follows `api-contract.md` exactly: paths, methods, field names, status codes and the local test settings. |

## Interfaces

Every interface between components or with external systems is defined as a contract in `docs/02_contracts/` in phase 2. The REST API is fixed by `api-contract.md` (AR-09); its phase 2 contract describes exactly that API.

| Interface | Between | Style (e.g. REST, gRPC, events, file, UI) |
|---|---|---|
| Registration form | participant and frontend | UI |
| Options, registration, export | frontend or organizer and backend | REST (OpenAPI) |
| Registration storage | backend and PostgreSQL | SQL (JPA) |
| JSON copy | backend and persistent volume | file (JSON schema) |
| Conference options | configuration and backend | file or configuration (schema defined in phase 2) |
| Emails | backend and SMTP server | SMTP |
| Anti-automation | frontend, backend and Google reCAPTCHA | JavaScript widget, HTTPS verify call |
# API contract

> Owner: Architect · Read in: phases 2, 3, 4, 6 · Agent: read-only

The REST API between the frontend or organizer and the backend is fixed by this file (AR-09): paths, methods, field names, status codes and the local test settings below are the same in every run of this project, so that external checks can use them. Everything not stated here (internal design, additional optional response fields, the OpenAPI document written in phase 2) is the agent's choice. The phase 2 contract in `docs/02_contracts/` must describe exactly this API.

## Local stack

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Backend base URL | `http://127.0.0.1:8080` (published by `02_output/docker-compose.yml`) |
| Mailpit web and API | `http://127.0.0.1:8025` |
| reCAPTCHA test mode | setting `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=true`; then the token `test-pass` is accepted and every other token is rejected |
| Rate limit | setting `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE`: requests per minute per client and endpoint; the agent chooses the default |
| Organizer HTTPS-only access | setting `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY`; `false` is allowed only on local plain HTTP |

`docker-compose.yml` passes these three settings from the environment to the backend, so they can be changed with `docker compose up` without editing a file. Organizer credentials are `ORGANIZER_USERNAME` and `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` from `.env`, sent with HTTP Basic authentication.

## Common rules

- Request and response bodies are JSON (`application/json; charset=utf-8`), except the export.
- Registration types are `EXTERNAL` and `STUDENT`; option categories are `WORKSHOP`, `EVENT`, `MEAL` and `OTHER`.
- Times are ISO 8601 with offset or `Z`.
- A rejected request (HTTP 400) has the body `{"errors": [{"field": "<name>", "message": "<text>"}]}`, one entry per invalid field. `field` is the request field's name as written in this file (for example `email`, `options`, `consents`, `captchaToken`); for a query parameter it is the parameter name.
- A request without valid organizer credentials on an organizer endpoint is answered with HTTP 401 and no registration data.
- A request over the rate limit (`RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE`) is answered with HTTP 429.

## Endpoints

### `GET /api/form-config` (public)

Response 200:

```json
{
  "options": [
    {"id": "ws-ai", "name": "AI workshop", "category": "WORKSHOP", "availableTo": ["EXTERNAL", "STUDENT"]}
  ],
  "consents": [
    {"id": "privacy", "text": "I agree that …", "mandatory": true}
  ],
  "captchaSiteKey": "…"
}
```

Lists only active options (AC-003-01).

### `POST /api/registrations` (public)

Request:

```json
{
  "type": "EXTERNAL",
  "firstName": "Ana",
  "lastName": "Novak",
  "email": "ana@example.org",
  "organization": "Example d.o.o.",
  "studyInstitution": null,
  "studyProgramme": null,
  "studentId": null,
  "options": ["ws-ai"],
  "consents": ["privacy"],
  "captchaToken": "test-pass"
}
```

- `organization` is required for `EXTERNAL`; `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme` and `studentId` are required for `STUDENT`. Fields of the other type are ignored.
- `options` lists the selected option ids; `consents` lists the ids of the consents given.

Responses: 201 `{"id": "<registration id>"}`; 400 with field errors; any other error status when the registration could not be stored (AC-005-03).

### `GET /api/export` (organizer)

Response 200: an Excel workbook (`application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`). The first sheet's first row holds these column headers, in this order, followed by one row per registration:

`id`, `type`, `firstName`, `lastName`, `email`, `organization`, `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme`, `studentId`, `options`, `consents`, `registeredAt`

`options` and `consents` are the ids separated by `, `; a cell that does not apply to the registration's type is empty. Response 401 without valid organizer credentials.
# Quality requirements

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phases 2, 6, 7 · Agent: read-only

Adds to `general/quality/` (definition of done, test strategy, severity scale); do not repeat those here.

## Non-functional requirements

| ID | Category (performance, availability, accessibility, localisation, usability, …) | Requirement | How it is checked |
|---|---|---|---|
| NFR-01 | Localisation | Names and other text with Slovenian characters (č, š, ž) survive the form, database, JSON copy, emails and Excel export unchanged. | an end-to-end test with such input |
| NFR-02 | Reliability | Stored registrations and JSON copies survive recreation of every container. | runtime demonstration: `docker compose down` then `up`, data still present |
| NFR-03 | Usability | The frontend validates fields before submission and shows the backend's field errors next to the fields. | component tests |
| NFR-04 | Availability | The backend reports health and readiness, and the containers use them in health checks. | runtime demonstration |

## Thresholds

These thresholds are the **quality gate** of the project: the same in every run, per component (backend, frontend), over the scope and with the tests defined in `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`. The agent works until each component meets them, then stops adding tests for that component (rules and stop rule: "Quality gate" in `measurement-scope.md`). The rows below are read by `tools/build-report.mjs`; keep the format `>= <number> %`.

| Measure | Threshold |
|---|---|
| Line coverage (all levels together) | >= 95 % |
| Mutation score (adjusted) | >= 90 % |
| Branch coverage | record only |

## Mutation scope

The paths or packages whose code is mutated, the same in every run of this project (default: all production code of the component). Selection rule: validation, security, persistence and business-rule code. Rules: `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`.

| Component | Paths or packages | Exclusions and reason |
|---|---|---|
| backend | `si.konferenca.registration.**` (all production code under the root package, including validation, security, persistence, business-rule, mail and export code) | The `@SpringBootApplication` entry-point class (no logic); generated code. Nothing else may be excluded. |
| frontend | `src/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx,vue}` (all production source of the frontend) | Test files, type-declaration files (`*.d.ts`), the bootstrap file that only mounts the app, generated code. Nothing else may be excluded. |

The scope is all production code of both components, so mutation scores are on the same basis in every run. It is the root package and the source folder, not a list of sub-packages, because the agent chooses the sub-packages in phase 2. Each component's full automated suite runs against it (`measurement-scope.md`, "Mutation score").

## Additional done criteria

| ID | Criterion | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| DoD-P01 | Against the running local stack: one external and one student registration succeed. | runtime demonstration log |
| DoD-P02 | Each registration is in PostgreSQL and has its JSON copy. | database query, file listing |
| DoD-P03 | The participant email and the organizer email (with the JSON attachment) arrive in Mailpit. | Mailpit API output |
| DoD-P04 | The organizer downloads a valid Excel workbook; the same request without organizer access is refused. | response codes, opened workbook |
| DoD-P05 | The production reCAPTCHA code path is tested against a mocked verification endpoint, including a rejected token. | test report |

## Overrides

None.
# Security requirements

> Owner: Security officer · Read in: phases 2, 6 · Agent: read-only

Adds to `general/security/security-baseline.md` (SB-01 … SB-14); do not repeat those here.

## Verification standard

| Component | Standard | Level | Reason if above the default |
|---|---|---|---|
| backend | OWASP ASVS 5.0 | Level 1 | |
| frontend | OWASP ASVS 5.0 | Level 1 | |

Level 1 is a deliberate choice: the only authentication is one organizer role for one export operation, and the personal data is contact and study data, not sensitive data. Where a requirement below is more specific than ASVS, it applies as well.

## Authentication and authorization

- Participants are anonymous; there are no participant accounts.
- One organizer role may export registrations (BR-08). The mechanism is decided in phase 2, using the organizer credentials from `secrets.env.example`; identity providers are out of scope.
- Everything else (options, registration) is public but protected by SR-01 and SR-03.

## Personal data

| Data item | Purpose | Retention | Shown/exported to |
|---|---|---|---|
| First and last name | identify the participant | `OQ-06` | organizers (email, export) |
| Email | confirmation and contact | `OQ-06` | participant, organizers |
| Organization / institution | attendance records | `OQ-06` | organizers |
| Study institution, programme, student ID | student registration | `OQ-06` | organizers |
| Selected options | plan workshops, events and meals | `OQ-06` | participant (confirmation), organizers |
| Consents given, with timestamp | proof of consent (SB-14) | `OQ-06` | organizers |

## Project requirements

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SR-01 | Every registration is protected by Google reCAPTCHA v2 and verified on the backend; the frontend check alone is never enough. |
| SR-02 | reCAPTCHA test mode is enabled only by environment configuration, never by default; production refuses to start with test mode on or with empty keys. |
| SR-03 | Every public `/api` endpoint (form configuration, registration, export) is rate limited per client, and request bodies have a size limit. |
| SR-04 | Option identifiers are checked against the active configured set (BR-04). |
| SR-05 | Email content is generated safely: user input cannot inject headers or markup. |
| SR-06 | Organizer credentials are never accepted over plain HTTP, except on localhost. |

# Architecture

> Owner: Architect · Read in: phases 0, 2, 4, 6, 7 · Agent: read-only

## Components

Each component gets its own folder and README in `02_output/`. Versions come only from `tech-stack.md`; reference its ids, never repeat a version here.

```yaml
components:
  - name: backend
    type: api
    folder: 02_output/backend
    platform: java
    build: maven-wrapper
    bootstrap: Maven wrapper plus a hand-written pom.xml whose parent is org.springframework.boot:spring-boot-starter-parent; root package si.konferenca.registration
    commands:          # ES-05; filled in phase 0 if left empty
      build:
      test:
      check:
      run:
    depends_on: []
    deploys_as: container image (eclipse-temurin base, non-root)
  - name: frontend
    type: web-app
    folder: 02_output/frontend
    platform: node
    build: vite
    bootstrap: hand-written package.json with the exact tech-stack.md versions and a committed package-lock.json (no project generator)
    commands:
      build:
      test:
      check:
      run:
    depends_on: [backend]
    deploys_as: container image (static files served by nginx)
```

The local stack (both components, PostgreSQL, mail catcher) is started with `02_output/docker-compose.yml`.

## Constraints

Checkable rules the code must respect (layering, allowed dependencies, patterns). Checked automatically in phase 6 where the stack allows (DoD-04).

| ID | Constraint |
|---|---|
| AR-01 | The frontend talks to the backend only through the REST API under `/api`. |
| AR-02 | The backend's internal architecture is not prescribed: the agent declares and justifies it in `docs/02_specification.md` and then writes ArchUnit rules that check exactly that declaration. |
| AR-03 | No package cycles in the backend (ArchUnit slice check). |
| AR-04 | Conference options change through configuration only, without code changes and without changing the fixed participant fields (BR-01). The mechanism is decided in phase 2. |
| AR-05 | A success response is sent only after both the database row and the JSON copy are written (BR-06, BR-07). |
| AR-06 | The database schema changes only through Flyway migrations (ES-08). |
| AR-07 | The frontend contains no secret; the reCAPTCHA site key is its only key and comes from configuration. |
| AR-09 | The REST API under `/api` follows `api-contract.md` exactly: paths, methods, field names, status codes and the local test settings. |

## Interfaces

Every interface between components or with external systems is defined as a contract in `docs/02_contracts/` in phase 2. The REST API is fixed by `api-contract.md` (AR-09); its phase 2 contract describes exactly that API.

| Interface | Between | Style (e.g. REST, gRPC, events, file, UI) |
|---|---|---|
| Registration form | participant and frontend | UI |
| Options, registration, export | frontend or organizer and backend | REST (OpenAPI) |
| Registration storage | backend and PostgreSQL | SQL (JPA) |
| JSON copy | backend and persistent volume | file (JSON schema) |
| Conference options | configuration and backend | file or configuration (schema defined in phase 2) |
| Emails | backend and SMTP server | SMTP |
| Anti-automation | frontend, backend and Google reCAPTCHA | JavaScript widget, HTTPS verify call |
# API contract

> Owner: Architect · Read in: phases 2, 3, 4, 6 · Agent: read-only

The REST API between the frontend or organizer and the backend is fixed by this file (AR-09): paths, methods, field names, status codes and the local test settings below are the same in every run of this project, so that external checks can use them. Everything not stated here (internal design, additional optional response fields, the OpenAPI document written in phase 2) is the agent's choice. The phase 2 contract in `docs/02_contracts/` must describe exactly this API.

## Local stack

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Backend base URL | `http://127.0.0.1:8080` (published by `02_output/docker-compose.yml`) |
| Mailpit web and API | `http://127.0.0.1:8025` |
| reCAPTCHA test mode | setting `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=true`; then the token `test-pass` is accepted and every other token is rejected |
| Rate limit | setting `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE`: requests per minute per client and endpoint; the agent chooses the default |
| Organizer HTTPS-only access | setting `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY`; `false` is allowed only on local plain HTTP |

`docker-compose.yml` passes these three settings from the environment to the backend, so they can be changed with `docker compose up` without editing a file. Organizer credentials are `ORGANIZER_USERNAME` and `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` from `.env`, sent with HTTP Basic authentication.

## Common rules

- Request and response bodies are JSON (`application/json; charset=utf-8`), except the export.
- Registration types are `EXTERNAL` and `STUDENT`; option categories are `WORKSHOP`, `EVENT`, `MEAL` and `OTHER`.
- Times are ISO 8601 with offset or `Z`.
- A rejected request (HTTP 400) has the body `{"errors": [{"field": "<name>", "message": "<text>"}]}`, one entry per invalid field. `field` is the request field's name as written in this file (for example `email`, `options`, `consents`, `captchaToken`); for a query parameter it is the parameter name.
- A request without valid organizer credentials on an organizer endpoint is answered with HTTP 401 and no registration data.
- A request over the rate limit (`RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE`) is answered with HTTP 429.

## Endpoints

### `GET /api/form-config` (public)

Response 200:

```json
{
  "options": [
    {"id": "ws-ai", "name": "AI workshop", "category": "WORKSHOP", "availableTo": ["EXTERNAL", "STUDENT"]}
  ],
  "consents": [
    {"id": "privacy", "text": "I agree that …", "mandatory": true}
  ],
  "captchaSiteKey": "…"
}
```

Lists only active options (AC-003-01).

### `POST /api/registrations` (public)

Request:

```json
{
  "type": "EXTERNAL",
  "firstName": "Ana",
  "lastName": "Novak",
  "email": "ana@example.org",
  "organization": "Example d.o.o.",
  "studyInstitution": null,
  "studyProgramme": null,
  "studentId": null,
  "options": ["ws-ai"],
  "consents": ["privacy"],
  "captchaToken": "test-pass"
}
```

- `organization` is required for `EXTERNAL`; `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme` and `studentId` are required for `STUDENT`. Fields of the other type are ignored.
- `options` lists the selected option ids; `consents` lists the ids of the consents given.

Responses: 201 `{"id": "<registration id>"}`; 400 with field errors; any other error status when the registration could not be stored (AC-005-03).

### `GET /api/export` (organizer)

Response 200: an Excel workbook (`application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet`). The first sheet's first row holds these column headers, in this order, followed by one row per registration:

`id`, `type`, `firstName`, `lastName`, `email`, `organization`, `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme`, `studentId`, `options`, `consents`, `registeredAt`

`options` and `consents` are the ids separated by `, `; a cell that does not apply to the registration's type is empty. Response 401 without valid organizer credentials.
# Quality requirements

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phases 2, 6, 7 · Agent: read-only

Adds to `general/quality/` (definition of done, test strategy, severity scale); do not repeat those here.

## Non-functional requirements

| ID | Category (performance, availability, accessibility, localisation, usability, …) | Requirement | How it is checked |
|---|---|---|---|
| NFR-01 | Localisation | Names and other text with Slovenian characters (č, š, ž) survive the form, database, JSON copy, emails and Excel export unchanged. | an end-to-end test with such input |
| NFR-02 | Reliability | Stored registrations and JSON copies survive recreation of every container. | runtime demonstration: `docker compose down` then `up`, data still present |
| NFR-03 | Usability | The frontend validates fields before submission and shows the backend's field errors next to the fields. | component tests |
| NFR-04 | Availability | The backend reports health and readiness, and the containers use them in health checks. | runtime demonstration |

## Thresholds

These thresholds are the **quality gate** of the project: the same in every run, per component (backend, frontend), over the scope and with the tests defined in `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`. The agent works until each component meets them, then stops adding tests for that component (rules and stop rule: "Quality gate" in `measurement-scope.md`). The rows below are read by `tools/build-report.mjs`; keep the format `>= <number> %`.

| Measure | Threshold |
|---|---|
| Line coverage (all levels together) | >= 95 % |
| Mutation score (adjusted) | >= 90 % |
| Branch coverage | record only |

## Mutation scope

The paths or packages whose code is mutated, the same in every run of this project (default: all production code of the component). Selection rule: validation, security, persistence and business-rule code. Rules: `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`.

| Component | Paths or packages | Exclusions and reason |
|---|---|---|
| backend | `si.konferenca.registration.**` (all production code under the root package, including validation, security, persistence, business-rule, mail and export code) | The `@SpringBootApplication` entry-point class (no logic); generated code. Nothing else may be excluded. |
| frontend | `src/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx,vue}` (all production source of the frontend) | Test files, type-declaration files (`*.d.ts`), the bootstrap file that only mounts the app, generated code. Nothing else may be excluded. |

The scope is all production code of both components, so mutation scores are on the same basis in every run. It is the root package and the source folder, not a list of sub-packages, because the agent chooses the sub-packages in phase 2. Each component's full automated suite runs against it (`measurement-scope.md`, "Mutation score").

## Additional done criteria

| ID | Criterion | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| DoD-P01 | Against the running local stack: one external and one student registration succeed. | runtime demonstration log |
| DoD-P02 | Each registration is in PostgreSQL and has its JSON copy. | database query, file listing |
| DoD-P03 | The participant email and the organizer email (with the JSON attachment) arrive in Mailpit. | Mailpit API output |
| DoD-P04 | The organizer downloads a valid Excel workbook; the same request without organizer access is refused. | response codes, opened workbook |
| DoD-P05 | The production reCAPTCHA code path is tested against a mocked verification endpoint, including a rejected token. | test report |

## Overrides

None.
# Security requirements

> Owner: Security officer · Read in: phases 2, 6 · Agent: read-only

Adds to `general/security/security-baseline.md` (SB-01 … SB-14); do not repeat those here.

## Verification standard

| Component | Standard | Level | Reason if above the default |
|---|---|---|---|
| backend | OWASP ASVS 5.0 | Level 1 | |
| frontend | OWASP ASVS 5.0 | Level 1 | |

Level 1 is a deliberate choice: the only authentication is one organizer role for one export operation, and the personal data is contact and study data, not sensitive data. Where a requirement below is more specific than ASVS, it applies as well.

## Authentication and authorization

- Participants are anonymous; there are no participant accounts.
- One organizer role may export registrations (BR-08). The mechanism is decided in phase 2, using the organizer credentials from `secrets.env.example`; identity providers are out of scope.
- Everything else (options, registration) is public but protected by SR-01 and SR-03.

## Personal data

| Data item | Purpose | Retention | Shown/exported to |
|---|---|---|---|
| First and last name | identify the participant | `OQ-06` | organizers (email, export) |
| Email | confirmation and contact | `OQ-06` | participant, organizers |
| Organization / institution | attendance records | `OQ-06` | organizers |
| Study institution, programme, student ID | student registration | `OQ-06` | organizers |
| Selected options | plan workshops, events and meals | `OQ-06` | participant (confirmation), organizers |
| Consents given, with timestamp | proof of consent (SB-14) | `OQ-06` | organizers |

## Project requirements

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SR-01 | Every registration is protected by Google reCAPTCHA v2 and verified on the backend; the frontend check alone is never enough. |
| SR-02 | reCAPTCHA test mode is enabled only by environment configuration, never by default; production refuses to start with test mode on or with empty keys. |
| SR-03 | Every public `/api` endpoint (form configuration, registration, export) is rate limited per client, and request bodies have a size limit. |
| SR-04 | Option identifiers are checked against the active configured set (BR-04). |
| SR-05 | Email content is generated safely: user input cannot inject headers or markup. |
| SR-06 | Organizer credentials are never accepted over plain HTTP, except on localhost. |
| SR-07 | The export and the organizer email expose only registration data, never internal fields or other system data. |
| SR-08 | The reverse proxy in front of the backend never forwards a client-supplied `Host` header; it sets the upstream host itself. |

## Overrides

None.

    <plugins>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
        <artifactId>spring-boot-maven-plugin</artifactId>

      </plugin>

        <artifactId>spotbugs-maven-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>${spotbugs-plugin.version}</version>
        <configuration>
          <effort>Max</effort>
          <threshold>Medium</threshold>
        </configuration>
      </plugin>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.jacoco</groupId>
        <artifactId>jacoco-maven-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>${jacoco.version}</version>
        <executions>
          <execution>
            <id>prepare-agent</id>
            <goals>
              <goal>prepare-agent</goal>
            </goals>
          </execution>
          <execution>
            <id>report</id>
            <phase>verify</phase>
            <goals>
              <goal>report</goal>
            </goals>
          </execution>
        </executions>
      </plugin>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.pitest</groupId>
        <artifactId>pitest-maven</artifactId>
        <version>${pitest.version}</version>
        <dependencies>
          <dependency>
            <groupId>org.pitest</groupId>
            <artifactId>pitest-junit5-plugin</artifactId>
            <version>${pitest-junit5.version}</version>
          </dependency>
        </dependencies>
        <configuration>
          <targetClasses>
            <param>si.konferenca.registration.*</param>
          </targetClasses>
          <targetTests>
            <param>si.konferenca.registration.*</param>
          </targetTests>
          <excludedClasses>
            <param>si.konferenca.registration.RegistrationApplication</param>
          </excludedClasses>
          <outputFormats>
            <format>HTML</format>
            <format>XML</format>
          </outputFormats>
          <timestampedReports>false</timestampedReports>
        </configuration>
      </plugin>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.owasp</groupId>
        <artifactId>dependency-check-maven</artifactId>
        <version>${dependency-check.version}</version>
        <configuration>
          <nvdApiKeyEnvironmentVariable>NVD_API_KEY</nvdApiKeyEnvironmentVariable>
          <formats>
            <format>HTML</format>
            <format>JSON</format>
          </formats>
        </configuration>
      </plugin>
    </plugins>
  </build>
</project>
