# User stories

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 6 · Agent: read-only

## Format

- Stories: `US-nnn`, "As a … I want … so that …", plus in-scope and out-of-scope notes.
- Acceptance criteria are given in `acceptance-criteria.md` as `AC-nnn-nn` (Given/When/Then), one observable behaviour each, each citing its `US` and any `BR`; the agent does not derive them.
- Do not invent behaviour a story does not state; record the gap as an `OQ` in `scope.md`.

## Stories

Epic: as a conference organizer, I want participants to register online, so that registrations are collected and managed reliably.

### US-001 External participant registration

As an external participant, I want to register using the external participant form, so that I can attend the conference and the activities I select.
In scope: the external form (BR-01), selecting active options (BR-04). Out of scope: payment, accounts, editing a submitted registration.

### US-002 Student registration

As a student, I want to register using the student form, so that I can attend the conference and the activities available to students.
In scope: the student form (BR-01), selecting active options (BR-04). Out of scope: verifying student status externally, accounts.

### US-003 Configurable conference options

As an organizer, I want workshops, events, meals and other optional activities to be configurable, so that the system can be reused when the programme changes.
Out of scope: an administration UI for options.

### US-004 Registration confirmation

As a participant, I want a clear confirmation in the application after my registration is processed, so that I know it was received (BR-06).

### US-005 Reliable registration storage

As an organizer, I want every accepted registration stored reliably, so that none is lost and each can be recovered (BR-07).

### US-006 Participant email confirmation

As a participant, I want an email confirming my registration, so that I have a record of it.

### US-007 Organizer notification

As an organizer, I want an email when someone registers, containing the submitted data with the raw registration JSON attached, so that I can monitor incoming registrations.

### US-008 Registration export

As an organizer, I want to export the current registrations as an Excel workbook, so that I can process them outside the system (BR-08).
# Business rules

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 6 · Agent: read-only

## Rules

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| BR-01 | There are two registration types: external participant and student. Each has the fixed fields listed under Data; configuration never changes them. |
| BR-02 | Required fields are never empty; leading and trailing whitespace is not significant. |
| BR-03 | Email has a valid email format. Text accepts Unicode, including Slovenian characters (č, š, ž). |
| BR-04 | Options are grouped as workshops, events, meals and other activities. Only active options can be selected; unknown or inactive options are rejected. |
| BR-05 | Mandatory consents must be given and are never preselected. |
| BR-06 | The in-application confirmation is shown only after the registration was accepted. |
| BR-07 | An accepted registration is stored in the database and as a raw JSON copy on persistent storage. |
| BR-08 | Only organizers can obtain the registration list; it is not reachable without organizer access. |

## Data

| Form or entity | Fields (all required) |
|---|---|
| External participant | first name, last name, email, organization / institution |
| Student | first name, last name, email, study institution, study programme, student ID |
| Conference option | stable identifier, display name, category (workshop, event, meal, other), active or inactive |
| Consent | which consents exist and their wording: `OQ-02` |

## Glossary

- Participant: a person who registers, external or student.
- Organizer: conference staff who receive notifications and export registrations.
- Option: a selectable workshop, event, meal or other activity.
- Active option: an option currently offered for selection.
- Raw JSON copy: the registration exactly as accepted, stored as a file for backup.
 Kept until the operator deletes them; no automatic deletion. The release notes tell the operator to delete the database rows and JSON copies no later than 12 months after the conference. |Allowed; each registration is stored separately and the export shows both. |No limit per category; each option at most once per registration, duplicates are rejected. |The registration stays accepted (HTTP 201, confirmation shown). Emails are sent only after the database row and the JSON copy exist; an email failure is logged with the registration id only, no personal data. |Consents are part of the conference configuration (id, wording, mandatory). The shipped configuration has one mandatory consent `privacy`: "I agree that my personal data is processed for organizing the conference and that it is shared with the conference organizers." |Every option carries a configured list of registration types it is available to (default: both); the backend rejects an option that is not available to the registration type. |# Scope

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 6 · Agent: read-only

## In scope

- Registration forms for external participants and students (US-001, US-002)
- Configurable conference options (US-003)
- In-application confirmation, participant confirmation email, organizer notification email with the JSON attachment (US-004, US-006, US-007)
- Storage in the database plus a raw JSON copy (US-005)
- Excel export for organizers (US-008)
- Anti-automation protection of the registration form

## Out of scope

- Participant accounts and login
- Payment processing
- Editing or cancelling a submitted registration
- Verifying student status externally
- An administration UI or dashboard, including option configuration
- Integration with an identity provider

## Priorities

1. A registration is never lost: storage (BR-07) comes before any notification.
2. Security and privacy (`project/02_design/security-requirements.md`) come before convenience.
3. The participant flow (US-001 to US-006) comes before organizer features (US-007, US-008).

## Open questions

| ID | Question | Owner | Answer |
|---|---|---|---|
| OQ-01 | Are all options available to students, or are some only for external participants? | Product owner | Every option carries a configured list of registration types it is available to (default: both); the backend rejects an option that is not available to the registration type. |
| OQ-02 | Which mandatory consents exist, and what is their wording? | Product owner | Consents are part of the conference configuration (id, wording, mandatory). The shipped configuration has one mandatory consent `privacy`: "I agree that my personal data is processed for organizing the conference and that it is shared with the conference organizers." |
| OQ-03 | What happens when storage succeeds but an email fails? | Product owner | The registration stays accepted (HTTP 201, confirmation shown). Emails are sent only after the database row and the JSON copy exist; an email failure is logged with the registration id only, no personal data. |
| OQ-04 | How many options may a participant select per category? | Product owner | No limit per category; each option at most once per registration, duplicates are rejected. |
| OQ-05 | Is a second registration with the same email allowed? | Product owner | Allowed; each registration is stored separately and the export shows both. |
| OQ-06 | How long are registrations and JSON copies kept? | Product owner | Kept until the operator deletes them; no automatic deletion. The release notes tell the operator to delete the database rows and JSON copies no later than 12 months after the conference. |

The answers are the product owner's decisions and hold for every run of this project; the agent records no decision for them. A new question that arises later becomes a decision record as usual.

- Configurable conference options (US-003)
- In-application confirmation, participant confirmation email, organizer notification email with the JSON attachment (US-004, US-006, US-007)
- Storage in the database plus a raw JSON copy (US-005)
- Excel export for organizers (US-008)
- Anti-automation protection of the registration form

## Out of scope

- Participant accounts and login
- Payment processing
- Editing or cancelling a submitted registration
- Verifying student status externally
- An administration UI or dashboard, including option configuration

1. A registration is never lost: storage (BR-07) comes before any notification.

| ID | Question | Owner | Answer |

The shipped configuration has one mandatory consent `privacy`: "I agree that my personal data is processed for organizing the conference and that it is shared with the conference organizers." |

content.content:
# Acceptance criteria

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 3, 6 · Agent: read-only

This list is an input, the same in every run of this project: the agent does not derive, add, merge or reword criteria. Each criterion states one observable behaviour (Given / When / Then) and cites its story and rules. "Rejected" always means: the API answers with an error status and field errors, no database row and no JSON copy are created, and no email is sent. The open questions are answered in `scope.md` (OQ-01 to OQ-06).

Common terms used below:

- *valid external submission*: registration type `EXTERNAL`; first name, last name, email, organization filled; every mandatory consent given; a reCAPTCHA token the verifier accepts; zero or more distinct active option ids available to the type.
- *valid student submission*: as above with type `STUDENT` and study institution, study programme and student ID instead of organization.

## US-001 External participant registration

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-001-01 | Given active options are configured, when a valid external submission is sent, then it is accepted (HTTP 201) and the response contains the new registration id. | BR-01, BR-04 |
| AC-001-02 | Given the external form, when any one required field (first name, last name, email, organization) is missing, empty or only whitespace, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for that field. | BR-01, BR-02 |
| AC-001-03 | Given a valid external submission whose text fields have leading and trailing spaces, when it is accepted, then the stored values have the spaces removed. | BR-02 |
| AC-001-04 | Given the external form, when the email does not have a valid email format, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for the email field. | BR-03 |
| AC-001-05 | Given the external form, when an option id is unknown, inactive or listed twice, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for the options. | BR-04, SR-04, OQ-04 |
| AC-001-06 | Given the external form, when a mandatory consent is not given, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for that consent. | BR-05, OQ-02 |
| AC-001-07 | Given the external form, when the reCAPTCHA token is missing or the verifier rejects it, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) and nothing is stored. | SR-01, scope (anti-automation) |
| AC-001-08 | Given the registration page, when the participant chooses "external participant", then the page shows exactly the external fields, the active options grouped as workshops, events, meals and other activities, and every consent checkbox unchecked. | BR-01, BR-04, BR-05 |

## US-002 Student registration

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-002-01 | Given active options are configured, when a valid student submission is sent, then it is accepted (HTTP 201) and the response contains the new registration id. | BR-01, BR-04 |
| AC-002-02 | Given the student form, when any one required field (first name, last name, email, study institution, study programme, student ID) is missing, empty or only whitespace, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for that field. | BR-01, BR-02 |
| AC-002-03 | Given the student form, when the email does not have a valid email format, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for the email field. | BR-03 |
| AC-002-04 | Given an active option configured as not available to students, when a student submission selects it, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for the options. | BR-04, OQ-01 |
| AC-002-05 | Given the student form, when a mandatory consent is not given, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for that consent. | BR-05, OQ-02 |
| AC-002-06 | Given the student form, when the reCAPTCHA token is missing or the verifier rejects it, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) and nothing is stored. | SR-01 |
| AC-002-07 | Given the registration page, when the participant chooses "student", then the page shows exactly the student fields and only the active options available to students, grouped by category, with every consent checkbox unchecked. | BR-01, BR-04, BR-05, OQ-01 |

## US-003 Configurable conference options

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-003-01 | Given a configuration with active and inactive options, when the form configuration is requested, then it lists only the active options, each with its identifier, display name, category and the registration types it is available to. | BR-04 |
| AC-003-02 | Given the backend is started with a different options configuration (an option added, one deactivated), when the form configuration is requested, then it reflects the new configuration, with no code change. | AR-04 |
| AC-003-03 | Given an options configuration that is invalid (duplicate identifier, unknown category, missing name), when the backend starts, then it refuses to start. | AR-04 |

## US-004 Registration confirmation

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-004-01 | Given a filled form, when the backend accepts the registration, then the page shows a confirmation with the participant's name and the selected options, and the form is no longer shown. | BR-06 |
| AC-004-02 | Given a filled form, when the backend rejects the registration with field errors, then no confirmation is shown, each error is shown next to its field, and the entered values remain. | BR-06, NFR-03 |
| AC-004-03 | Given a form with an empty required field or an invalid email, when the participant submits, then the page shows the field errors and sends no request to the backend. | NFR-03 |
| AC-004-04 | Given a filled form, when the backend fails or cannot be reached, then no confirmation is shown and a general error message without technical details is shown. | BR-06, SB-07 |

## US-005 Reliable registration storage

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-005-01 | Given a valid submission, when it is accepted, then the database holds one registration with the type, every submitted field, the selected options, each consent with the time it was given, and the time of registration. | BR-07 |
| AC-005-02 | Given a valid submission, when it is accepted, then a JSON copy named after the registration id exists in the JSON copy directory and contains the registration as accepted. | BR-07 |
| AC-005-03 | Given the JSON copy cannot be written, when a valid submission is sent, then the API answers with an error (not 201) and no registration is left in the database. | BR-07, AR-05 |
| AC-005-04 | Given a valid submission with Slovenian characters (č, š, ž, Č, Š, Ž) in the names and institution, when it is accepted, then the database row and the JSON copy contain the text unchanged. | BR-03, NFR-01 |

## US-006 Participant email confirmation

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-006-01 | Given a valid submission, when it is accepted, then one email is sent to the participant's address naming the conference, the participant and the selected options. | US-006 |
| AC-006-02 | Given a submission whose text fields contain line breaks, header-like text or HTML markup, when the confirmation email is sent, then the email has no additional headers or recipients and the markup appears only as literal text. | SR-05 |
| AC-006-03 | Given the mail server is unavailable, when a valid submission is sent, then the registration is still accepted (HTTP 201) and stored. | OQ-03, OQ-03 |

## US-007 Organizer notification

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-007-01 | Given organizer addresses are configured, when a registration is accepted, then each organizer address receives a notification email containing the submitted registration data. | US-007 |
| AC-007-02 | Given a registration is accepted, when the organizer notification is sent, then it has a JSON attachment whose content equals the stored JSON copy. | US-007, BR-07, SR-07 |

## US-008 Registration export

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-008-01 | Given stored registrations, when an organizer requests the export with valid organizer credentials, then the response is an Excel workbook (`.xlsx`) with one row per registration, containing its type, fields, selected options, consents and registration time. | BR-08 |
| AC-008-02 | Given stored registrations, when the export is requested without credentials or with wrong credentials, then it is refused (HTTP 401) and no registration data is returned. | BR-08, SB-02 |
| AC-008-03 | Given a registration with Slovenian characters, when the organizer exports, then the workbook cell contains the text unchanged. | NFR-01 |
| AC-008-04 | Given organizer HTTPS-only access is on, when the export is requested with valid credentials over plain HTTP from a client that is not on localhost, then it is refused and no registration data is returned. | SR-06 |

## Traceability

| Story | Criteria |
|---|---|
| US-001 | AC-001-01 … AC-001-08 |
| US-002 | AC-002-01 … AC-002-07 |
| US-003 | AC-003-01 … AC-003-03 |
| US-004 | AC-004-01 … AC-004-04 |
| US-005 | AC-005-01 … AC-005-04 |
| US-006 | AC-006-01 … AC-006-03 |
| US-007 | AC-007-01, AC-007-02 |
| US-008 | AC-008-01 … AC-008-04 |

Total: 35 criteria.

Requirements without their own criterion, covered in the specification and verified in phase 6: SR-03 rate and size limits, NFR-02 persistence across container recreation, NFR-04 health and readiness (runtime demonstration).
# End-to-end scenarios

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 3, 6 · Agent: read-only

The end-to-end tests of this project: exactly one test per scenario below, run against the real local stack (`docker compose up`: frontend, backend, PostgreSQL, Mailpit) through the browser, and the same in every run of this project. The agent writes no other end-to-end test and no scenario is merged or split. Each scenario names the criteria it demonstrates; the acceptance tests (one or more per criterion) carry the detailed cases, so an end-to-end test checks the journey once and does not repeat them.

| ID | Scenario | Steps and observations | Covers |
|---|---|---|---|
| E2E-01 | External participant registers | Open the page, choose "external participant", fill the form with valid data, select at least one option per category, submit. The page shows the confirmation. The database holds the registration, the JSON copy exists, the participant email and the organizer email (with the JSON attachment) are in Mailpit. | AC-001-01, AC-001-08, AC-004-01, AC-005-01, AC-005-02, AC-006-01, AC-007-01, AC-007-02, DoD-P01 to DoD-P03 |
| E2E-02 | Student registers | As E2E-01 with "student": only the student fields and student-available options are shown; the registration is stored and both emails arrive. | AC-002-01, AC-002-07, AC-004-01, DoD-P01 to DoD-P03 |
| E2E-03 | Field errors are shown next to the fields | Submit the form with an empty required field and an invalid email: errors appear next to the fields and no request reaches the backend; then make the backend reject a submission (for example an unavailable option): the backend's field errors appear next to their fields and the entered values remain. | AC-004-02, AC-004-03, NFR-03 |
| E2E-04 | Slovenian characters survive the whole chain | Register with č, š, ž, Č, Š, Ž in the names and institution. The text is unchanged in the page confirmation, the database row, the JSON copy, both emails and the exported workbook. | AC-005-04, AC-008-03, NFR-01 |
| E2E-05 | Organizer exports registrations | Request the export with valid organizer credentials: a valid Excel workbook with one row per registration is downloaded. The same request without credentials is refused (HTTP 401) and returns no data. | AC-008-01, AC-008-02, DoD-P04 |

Not end-to-end tests (verified by runtime demonstration in phase 6): NFR-02 (data survives recreation of every container) and NFR-04 (health and readiness).

# Definition of Done

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phases 6, 7 · Agent: read-only

Applies to every project; project additions are `DoD-Pnn` in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md`.
Each item needs evidence in `docs/06_verification-report.md`.

| ID | Criterion | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| DoD-01 | The full test suite passes; frozen test hashes match the manifest | test report, hash check |
| DoD-02 | Format, lint, type check and static analysis report no errors | tool output |
| DoD-03 | The quality gate of `general/quality/measurement-scope.md` ("Quality gate") is met for each component, or the shortfall after the third survivor round is recorded with a decision | coverage and mutation reports with scope, raw and adjusted score, rounds |
| DoD-04 | Architecture constraints (`AR`) are checked automatically where possible; no dependency cycles | architecture test output |
| DoD-05 | No open Critical or High finding from the security review and scanners | `general/skills/verify-release` output |
| DoD-06 | Every component runs in its target environment and the core user flows work at runtime, not only in tests | runtime demonstration log |
| DoD-07 | Every AC traces to at least one test and one commit | traceability table |
| DoD-08 | Root and component READMEs (ES-06) work when followed from a clean checkout | clone log |
| DoD-09 | Release notes list everything a human must test manually | `docs/release-notes.md` |
| DoD-10 | Every decision has a resolution or is listed as pending review; inputs and protected files are unchanged | decisions log, `docs/00_input-manifest.sha256` check |
| DoD-11 | The evidence checks in `general/phases.md` hold | `general/phases.md`, "Evidence" |
# Test strategy

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: every phase that writes or runs tests · Agent: read-only

When each test level is written and whether it is frozen is defined in `general/phases.md`. Project thresholds are in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md`.

## Constraints

- Do not test acceptance behaviour through internals; use the component's public interface (API, UI, CLI, messages).
- Do not depend on live external services in automated tests; use the local substitutes in `project/00_setup/environments.md` and list the real services in the release notes for manual testing.
- Do not leave flaky, skipped or disabled tests; fix them or record a decision.
- Do not weaken an assertion to make an incorrect implementation pass.
- Test names contain the AC id they verify.

## First complete run

Record the result of the first full run before fixing anything, then classify each failure:

| Class | Action |
|---|---|
| Implementation defect | fix the code |
| Defect in a non-frozen test | fix the test and say so in `docs/03_test-strategy.md` |
| Frozen test appears wrong | blocking decision; do not touch the test |

## Measures (recorded in every project)

Test counts, coverage, mutation score and code size are defined in `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`: what each covers, at which level and with which tool.

## Manifest

`docs/03_acceptance-manifest.sha256` uses `sha256sum` format with paths relative to `02_output/`, hashed after LF normalisation.
# Measurement scope

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phases 3, 5, 6 · Agent: read-only

Defines what test counts, coverage, mutation score and code size mean, so that figures from different runs compare. Record every figure in `run-log.json` → `codeMetrics` and in `docs/06_verification-report.md` with its scope, level and tool. The project selects paths and exclusions in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md` ("Mutation scope"); this file never names them.

## Constraints

- Do not change a tool's scope, filters, exclusions or thresholds to improve a number. A change is a decision record.
- Do not report a figure without its scope, level and tool.
- Production code is the source a component ships. It excludes tests, generated code, the application entry point and anything listed under "Measurement exclusions" in `docs/03_test-strategy.md` with a reason. Decide the exclusions in phase 3, before any test is written; do not extend them later.
- Test code never counts towards coverage or mutation.

## Test counts

Per component and level (`unit`, `integration`, `acceptance`, `architecture`, `e2e`), passed and failed, from the runner's own report.

## Coverage

Line and branch, per component, as three figures: `unit` (unit tests only), `nonUnit` (integration, acceptance and end-to-end tests that exercise the component) and `all` (one merged report). The headline figure is `all`.

## Mutation score

- **Scope:** all production code of the component, narrowed only to the paths in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md` "Mutation scope", which are the same in every run of the project (default: all production code). Do not narrow it by running only some tests or by excluding packages that are not listed there.
- **Tests:** the component's full automated suite, at every level it has, so the score does not depend on which level the agent ran. If that is infeasible, record the tests actually run and the reason in a decision record.
- **Record:** `{score, scoreAdjusted, scoreCovered, killed, equivalent, total, covered, scope, tests, tool, excluded}`. `score` (raw) = killed (timed-out counts as killed) ÷ all mutants the tool generated; a mutant no test reaches counts as survived. `scoreAdjusted` = (killed + equivalent) ÷ total, where `equivalent` is the number of survivors justified as equivalent. `scoreCovered` = killed ÷ mutants a test reaches.
- Do not remove equivalent mutants by hand. List every survivor you count as equivalent in `docs/03_test-strategy.md` with the class and method, the mutation and the reason it cannot change behaviour; a survivor without that entry is not equivalent. Always record the raw score next to the adjusted score.

## Code size

`cloc` (same version in every run): production = non-test source and resources, test = test sources including end-to-end tests. Generated code and lock files are excluded.

## Mutation run discipline

- Measure coverage and mutation score in phase 5, so that surviving mutants are handled before verification. Phase 6 repeats a measurement only for a component whose code or tests changed since, and only once, after the last fix.
- Do not start a full mutation run on code that is not final. One full run per component per measurement; the only other runs are the targeted survivor rounds and, only when the rule below requires it, one confirming full run.
- Check once, before the full run, that the tool works: a mutant in code the tests plainly cover must be killed. A score far below the line coverage (for example 25 % at 100 % coverage) means the tool is not activating mutants (known case: Stryker with the wrong Vitest major version); stop and raise a decision, do not record the figure.
- Start a long run in the background and continue with other checks of the phase; read its log only for the summary lines. Do not hold the session in a blocking wait on it.

## Quality gate

The gate is the same in every run of the project: the thresholds in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md` ("Thresholds"), per component, over the scope and with the tests defined above. It makes runs comparable: every run reaches the same quality, and what differs is the cost of reaching it.

- **Gate:** line coverage (`all`) at or above the line threshold, and `scoreAdjusted` at or above the mutation threshold. Branch coverage is recorded only.
- **Order in phase 5:** write the unit and integration tests area by area and measure line coverage after each area (fast) until the line threshold is met; then run mutation testing **once** per component (full run); then, if `scoreAdjusted` is below the threshold, up to **three** survivor rounds: each adds tests aimed at the survivors in the code that matters most (validation, security, persistence, business rules first) and re-runs only the mutated classes. After each round recompute `scoreAdjusted` for the component from the last full run plus the re-run classes (the classes that were not re-run keep their killed and total counts from the full run) and write the per-class numbers into `docs/03_test-strategy.md`. If the recomputed score is at least 1.0 point above the threshold the gate is met and no full run follows. Only a recomputed score less than 1.0 point above the threshold, or a change to a class outside the re-run set, needs the one confirming full run; its result then replaces the recomputed one.
- **Stop at the gate:** once a component meets both thresholds, add no further test and start no further mutation run for it. Do not add tests for coverage or score beyond the gate.
- **Shortfall:** after the third round a component still below a threshold is recorded as a shortfall (which threshold, by how many points) in a non-blocking decision and as a finding, and the run continues. Do not change the scope, the tests run or the exclusions to reach a threshold; that is a decision record at most.
- **Record in `run-log.json`:** `codeMetrics.gate` = `{ thresholds: {lineCoverage, mutationScore}, perComponent: { <name>: { lineMet, mutationMet, lineShortfall, mutationShortfall } }, mutationRounds: { <name>: n }, testsAtFirstMutation: { <name>: n }, met: true|false }`; `mutationRounds` is 0 when the first full run already met the gate.

# Specification

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: `project/01_requirements/acceptance-criteria.md`, `project/00_setup/tech-stack.md`, `project/00_setup/environments.md`, `project/02_design/*`, `general/security/*` · Agent: writes

Conference registration: participants register through a React form; a Spring Boot API validates, stores (PostgreSQL row + JSON copy), mails and exports registrations. Versions: `tech-stack.md` as amended by D-09. Contracts: [`02_contracts/`](02_contracts/).

## 1. Components and deployment

| Component | Folder | Runs as | Local port (127.0.0.1 only) |
|---|---|---|---|
| backend | `02_output/backend` | `eclipse-temurin` JRE image, user `app` (uid 10001), jar built by `./mvnw package` | 8080 |
| frontend | `02_output/frontend` | multi-stage: `node` image builds, `nginx` image serves `dist/` as user `nginx` on port 8080 | 3000 |
| postgres | image | `postgres` image, database and user `registration`, named volume `pgdata` | not published |
| mailpit | image | `axllent/mailpit`, SMTP 1025 inside the network | 8025 (web and API) |

- `02_output/docker-compose.yml` starts all four; JSON copies live on the named volume `json-copies` mounted at `/data/json-copies` (NFR-02). Health checks: backend `wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:8080/actuator/health/readiness`, frontend `wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz`, postgres `pg_isready`; `depends_on: condition: service_healthy` orders start-up (NFR-04, ES-09).
- nginx serves `/` from the build and proxies `/api/` to `http://backend:8080` with `proxy_set_header Host backend:8080` (never the client's `Host`, SR-08), `X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr`, `X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme`; it adds the frontend security headers (section 7). Production puts the external TLS proxy in front (`environments.md`); its `Host` rule is in the release notes.
- `docker-compose.yml` passes `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE` (default `true`), `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` (default `30`) and `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY` (default `false`, local plain HTTP) from the environment, plus the `.env` secrets via `--env-file .env` (AR-09).

## 2. Backend architecture (AR-02, AR-03)

Ports-and-adapters with four layers under `si.konferenca.registration`. Reason: the rules that matter (validation, storage order, captcha) stay framework-free and testable, and each external system (database, file, SMTP, Google, Excel) sits behind one port, so test substitutes replace only adapters.

| Package | Contains | May depend on |
|---|---|---|
| `domain` | records and enums (`Registration`, `RegistrationType`, `OptionCategory`, `ConferenceOption`, `ConsentDefinition`, `ConferenceCatalog`, `FieldError`), `RegistrationValidator`, `ConferenceConfigException` | `java..` only |
| `application` | use cases `RegisterParticipant`, `RegistrationStorage` (transactional), `FormConfiguration`, `ExportRegistrations`; ports `RegistrationRepository`, `JsonCopyStore`, `CaptchaVerifier`, `RegistrationNotifier`, `WorkbookWriter`; exceptions `RegistrationRejectedException`, `StorageFailedException` | `domain`, `java..`, `org.slf4j..`, `org.springframework.stereotype..`, `org.springframework.transaction..` |
| `adapter.persistence`, `adapter.jsoncopy`, `adapter.mail`, `adapter.captcha`, `adapter.export`, `adapter.catalog` | JPA entities and repositories, file writer, mail sender, test-mode and Google verifiers, POI workbook writer, configuration loader | `application`, `domain`, frameworks; never `web` or another adapter |
| `web` | REST controllers, DTOs, `ApiExceptionHandler`, `RateLimitFilter`, `RequestSizeFilter` | `application`, `domain`, frameworks; never `adapter` |
| `config` | `AppProperties` (`@ConfigurationProperties("app")`), `StartupGuard`, `SecurityConfig`, `OrganizerHttpsOnlyFilter`, bean wiring | everything (composition root) |

ArchUnit rules (`architecture` tests, phase 3 freezes none of them; written in phase 5 as architecture tests): exactly the "May depend on" column, plus `slices().matching("si.konferenca.registration.(*)..").should().beFreeOfCycles()` (AR-03) and "`web` does not access `jakarta.persistence`" .

## 3. Configuration (ES-01, AR-04)

Spring profiles `local` (compose) and `test` (automated tests) are the only environments where defaults marked "local/test" apply; production runs without a profile. Property names are under `app.` and bound from the environment variables below.

| Environment variable | Property | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DB_URL`, `DB_USERNAME`, `DB_PASSWORD` | `spring.datasource.*` | local/test only (`jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/registration`, `registration`) | compose maps `DB_PASSWORD` from `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`; no password default |
| `MAIL_HOST`, `MAIL_PORT`, `MAIL_TLS` | `spring.mail.host`, `.port`, `mail.smtp.starttls.enable/required` | local/test only (`localhost`, `1025`, `false`); production default TLS `true` | connect/read/write timeouts 5 s |
| `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` | `spring.mail.username/password` | empty | production only |
| `MAIL_FROM` | `app.mail.from` | `registration@konferenca.example` | |
| `CONFERENCE_NAME` | `app.conference.name` | `Conference` | used in email subjects and bodies |
| `CONFERENCE_CONFIG` | `app.conference.config-location` | local/test only: `classpath:conference-config.json` | Spring resource location (`file:/…` in production) |
| `JSON_COPY_DIR` | `app.json-copy.directory` | `/data/json-copies` | created on first write, not at start |
| `CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE` | `app.captcha.test-mode` | `false` | `true` only in profiles local/test (startup guard) |
| `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`, `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` | `app.captcha.site-key`, `.secret-key` | empty | required when test mode is off |
| `RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL` | `app.captcha.verify-url` | `https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify` | tests point it to a mock |
| `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`, `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` | `app.organizer.username`, `.password` | none (required) | password hashed with BCrypt at start; only the hash is kept (SB-03) |
| `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` | `app.organizer.emails` | none (required) | comma separated |
| `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY` | `app.organizer.https-only` | `true` | `false` only in profiles local/test |
| `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN` | `app.cors.allowed-origin` | empty (no CORS) | non-empty only in profile local |
| `RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` | `app.rate-limit.per-minute` | `30` | per client address and endpoint |
| `MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` | `app.request.max-bytes` | `16384` | |

**Startup guard** (`StartupGuard`, runs before the web server accepts requests): the backend refuses to start (context fails) when (a) test mode is on outside local/test, (b) test mode is off and a reCAPTCHA key is empty, (c) `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY=false` or `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN` is set outside local/test, (d) organizer username, password or emails are empty, (e) the conference configuration is missing or invalid (AC-003-03).

**Conference configuration** (AR-04, US-003): a JSON file following [`conference-config.schema.json`](02_contracts/conference-config.schema.json), read once at start by `adapter.catalog.JsonConferenceCatalogLoader` into a `domain.ConferenceCatalog`. Validation in `ConferenceCatalog` (domain): duplicate option id, duplicate consent id, unknown category or type, blank id/name/text, empty `availableTo` → `ConferenceConfigException` → start fails. Another file plus a restart changes the options without a code change (AC-003-02). The shipped `classpath:conference-config.json` contains:

| id | name | category | availableTo | active |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ws-ai` | AI workshop | WORKSHOP | both | yes |
| `ws-security` | Secure coding workshop | WORKSHOP | both | yes |
| `ev-reception` | Welcome reception | EVENT | both | yes |
| `ev-industry-tour` | Industry tour | EVENT | EXTERNAL | yes |
| `meal-lunch` | Lunch | MEAL | both | yes |
| `meal-dinner` | Conference dinner | MEAL | EXTERNAL | yes |
| `other-certificate` | Certificate of attendance | OTHER | both | yes |
| `ws-legacy` | Legacy systems workshop | WORKSHOP | both | no |

and one consent `privacy` (mandatory) with the wording of OQ-02.

## 4. REST API (AR-09, `api-contract.md`)

Exactly [`openapi.json`](02_contracts/openapi.json). Responses carry `Content-Type: application/json;charset=UTF-8` (`server.servlet.encoding.force-response=true`).

### `GET /api/form-config`
Active options only, each with `id`, `name`, `category`, `availableTo` (AC-003-01); all consents; `captchaSiteKey`; additional field `captchaTestMode`.

### `POST /api/registrations` — validation (`domain.RegistrationValidator`, SB-01)
All checks run and every failing field gets one entry (first failing rule per field), so the frontend can show them together.

| Field | Rule (in order) | Message |
|---|---|---|
| body | unreadable JSON or wrong JSON types → only this error | `Request body is not valid JSON.` |
| `type` | missing or not `EXTERNAL`/`STUDENT` (D-13) → only this error | `Registration type must be EXTERNAL or STUDENT.` |
| `firstName`, `lastName`, `email`, and `organization` (EXTERNAL) or `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme`, `studentId` (STUDENT) | trimmed (`String.strip()`, BR-02); null/empty after trim → required; longer than 200 (email 254) code points → too long (D-12) | `This field is required.` / `This value is too long.` |
| `email` | after trim must match `^[A-Za-z0-9.!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{\|}~-]+@[A-Za-z0-9](?:[A-Za-z0-9-]{0,61}[A-Za-z0-9])?(?:\.[A-Za-z0-9](?:[A-Za-z0-9-]{0,61}[A-Za-z0-9])?)+$` (BR-03; no whitespace, CR or LF) | `Enter a valid email address.` |
| fields of the other type | ignored, stored as null | — |
| `options` | null = none; an id listed twice (OQ-04), unknown, inactive (BR-04, SR-04) or not available to the type (OQ-01) → one error naming the first offending id | `Option '<id>' is not available.` / `Option '<id>' is selected more than once.` |
| `consents` | a mandatory consent missing (BR-05) or an id not in the configuration (D-11); duplicates collapse | `Consent '<id>' is required.` / `Consent '<id>' is unknown.` |
| `captchaToken` | null/blank → required; otherwise `CaptchaVerifier.verify(token)` false → rejected; verified only when every other field is valid | `This field is required.` / `The reCAPTCHA check failed. Please try again.` |

Any error → HTTP 400 `{"errors":[…]}`, nothing stored, no email (AC-001-02..07, AC-002-02..06).

### `POST /api/registrations` — acceptance flow (AR-05, BR-07, OQ-03)
1. `RegisterParticipant` validates and verifies the captcha.
2. `RegistrationStorage.store` (`@Transactional`): creates `Registration` (UUID, `registeredAt` = now truncated to milliseconds UTC, every given consent with `givenAt = registeredAt`), saves it through `RegistrationRepository` and flushes, then `JsonCopyStore.write` serialises it to [`registration-copy.schema.json`](02_contracts/registration-copy.schema.json) and writes `<id>.json` (temp file in the same directory, then atomic move). An exception rolls the row back; a rollback after the file was written deletes the file (transaction synchronisation). Any storage failure → `StorageFailedException` → HTTP 500 `{"message":"The registration could not be stored. Please try again later."}` (AC-005-03).
3. After the commit, `RegistrationNotifier` sends the participant confirmation and one organizer notification per address ([`emails.json`](02_contracts/emails.json)), synchronously with 5 s timeouts; each failure is caught and logged as `Email for registration <id> failed` only (no personal data, ES-07).
4. HTTP 201 `{"id":"<uuid>"}` with `Location`.

### `GET /api/export` (BR-08, US-008)
`ExportRegistrations` reads every registration ordered by `registeredAt`, `id`; `adapter.export.PoiWorkbookWriter` writes an XSSF workbook, sheet `Registrations`, header row of the 12 contract columns, one row per registration, all string cells (no formula evaluation of user text), `options`/`consents` joined by `, `, non-applicable cells empty, `registeredAt` as `Instant.toString()`. `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="registrations.xlsx"`.

### Errors (SB-07, ES-07)
`ApiExceptionHandler`: 400 as above; 404/405/415 and every unexpected exception → `{"message": "<generic text>"}` without stack traces, class names or SQL; Spring's whitelabel and `server.error.include-*` disabled. Log lines carry the registration id or request path, never field values.

## 5. Security (SB-01..SB-11, SR-01..SR-08, ASVS 5.0 L1)

- **Organizer access (SB-02, BR-08, SR-06, SR-07)**: Spring Security, stateless, HTTP Basic with one in-memory user (`ROLE_ORGANIZER`, BCrypt hash, SB-03). `/api/export` requires the role; `GET /api/form-config`, `POST /api/registrations`, `GET /actuator/health/**` are public; everything else is denied. Wrong or missing credentials → 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="organizer"` and no body data. `OrganizerHttpsOnlyFilter` runs after authentication on `/api/export`: when `https-only` is on, the request is not secure (`request.isSecure()`, with `server.forward-headers-strategy=native` honouring `X-Forwarded-Proto` from trusted internal proxies) and the client address is not loopback → 403 `{"message":"Organizer access requires HTTPS."}`, no data (AC-008-04). CSRF is disabled (no cookies or sessions; Basic credentials are not sent automatically cross-site by the form).
- **reCAPTCHA (SR-01, SR-02, DoD-P05)**: [`recaptcha.json`](02_contracts/recaptcha.json). `adapter.captcha.TestModeCaptchaVerifier` (token `test-pass`) or `GoogleCaptchaVerifier` (Spring `RestClient`, form POST to `app.captcha.verify-url`) selected by `app.captcha.test-mode`; the Google path is tested against a mock HTTP server, accepted and rejected token.
- **Rate and size limits (SR-03, SB-06)**: `RateLimitFilter` — fixed one-minute window per (client address, endpoint `METHOD path`) for every `/api/**` request, including failed logins; over the limit → 429 with `Retry-After`; old windows evicted. Client address = `request.getRemoteAddr()` after the native forward-header handling. `RequestSizeFilter` — `Content-Length` above `max-bytes` → 413; bodies without a length are read through a counting stream that fails at the limit → 413.
- **Input and output (SB-01, SB-05, SR-04, SR-05)**: server-side validation above; JPA with bound parameters; option ids checked against the active set; emails plain text, fixed subjects, no user text in headers; the export writes string cells.
- **Headers (SB-10)**: backend — `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `Cache-Control: no-store`. Frontend nginx — `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://www.google.com/recaptcha/ https://www.gstatic.com/recaptcha/; frame-src https://www.google.com/recaptcha/ https://recaptcha.google.com/recaptcha/; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, plus `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: same-origin`; `server_tokens off`. (`'unsafe-inline'` for styles only: the reCAPTCHA widget sets inline styles.)
- **CORS**: none by default; `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN` (local only) allows that origin for `/api/**` GET/POST.
- **TLS (SB-04)**: outside the machine through the external reverse proxy (`environments.md`); organizer access enforced as above.
- **Least privilege (SB-11)**: both images run as non-root users; the database user owns only its database.
- **Secrets (SB-03, ES-02)**: only from the environment / `.env`; no defaults in code; `.env` git-ignored.
- **Scanning (SB-08, SB-09)**: Dependency-Check, `npm audit`, Semgrep, Gitleaks, SpotBugs, PMD in phase 6.
- **Personal data (SB-12..SB-14)**: exactly the fields of `security-requirements.md` "Personal data"; retention OQ-06 (operator deletes rows and copies at most 12 months after the conference, stated in the release notes); consents never preselected, stored with `givenAt`.

## 6. Storage (BR-07, AR-06, ES-08, NFR-01)

[`database.json`](02_contracts/database.json): Flyway migration `V1__create_registration_tables.sql`; `spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=validate`. JPA entity `RegistrationEntity` with element collections for options (ordered) and consents. Database encoding UTF8; the JSON copy is UTF-8 written by Jackson; mails UTF-8; POI strings are Unicode — Slovenian characters survive every step.

## 7. Frontend (US-001..US-004, NFR-03, AR-01, AR-07)

React 19 single page following [`ui-registration-form.json`](02_contracts/ui-registration-form.json).

| Module | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `src/api/client.ts` | `fetchFormConfig()`, `submitRegistration(payload)` → `{kind:'created',id} \| {kind:'invalid',errors} \| {kind:'failed'}`; relative `/api/...` URLs only |
| `src/domain/validation.ts` | client rules mirroring section 4 (required after trim, email pattern, lengths, mandatory consents, captcha) |
| `src/domain/payload.ts` | builds the request: trimmed values, only the fields of the chosen type, selected option ids in display order, consent ids, token |
| `src/components/RegistrationForm.tsx` | type chooser, fields, option groups, consents, captcha, submit, field and general errors |
| `src/components/OptionGroups.tsx`, `Captcha.tsx`, `Confirmation.tsx` | as named |
| `src/App.tsx` | loads the configuration, shows loading/error, form or confirmation |

Behaviour: no type chosen → only the chooser; choosing a type shows exactly that type's fields and the active options available to it grouped by category (AC-001-08, AC-002-07); client validation blocks the request (AC-004-03); 400 → backend errors next to fields, values kept (AC-004-02); 201 → confirmation with the participant's name and selected option names, form removed (AC-004-01); other status or network error → general error, no details (AC-004-04). The only key in the frontend is the site key from `/api/form-config` (AR-07). Dev server proxies `/api` to `127.0.0.1:8080`; production nginx proxies `/api/` (section 1).

## 8. Tests and measurement

Levels, tools and locations (frozen in phase 3; `general/phases.md`):

| Level | Backend | Frontend |
|---|---|---|
| acceptance | `src/test/java/si/konferenca/registration/acceptance/**` — JUnit 6 + Spring Boot test + MockMvc, PostgreSQL and Mailpit through Testcontainers, a JDK `HttpServer` as the reCAPTCHA mock | `tests/acceptance/**` — Vitest + Testing Library + jsdom, `fetch` stubbed |
| e2e | — | `e2e/**` — Playwright (Chromium) against `docker compose up` (frontend `http://127.0.0.1:3000`, backend `:8080`, Mailpit `:8025`), one test per E2E-01..05 |
| unit / integration / architecture | phase 5, `src/test/java/...` outside `acceptance` | phase 5, `src/**/*.test.ts(x)` |

Coverage JaCoCo / V8, mutation PIT / Stryker over the scopes of `quality-requirements.md`.

## Traceability

| `ev-industry-tour` | Industry tour | EVENT | EXTERNAL | yes |

and one consent `privacy` (mandatory) with the wording of OQ-02.

## 4. REST API (AR-09, `api-contract.md`)

Exactly [`openapi.json`](02_contracts/openapi.json). Responses carry `Content-Type: application/json;charset=UTF-8` (`server.servlet.encoding.force-response=true`).

### `GET /api/form-config`
Active options only, each with `id`, `name`, `category`, `availableTo` (AC-003-01); all consents; `captchaSiteKey`; additional field `captchaTestMode`.

### `POST /api/registrations` — validation (`domain.RegistrationValidator`, SB-01)
All checks run and every failing field gets one entry (first failing rule per field), so the frontend can show them together.

| Field | Rule (in order) | Message |
|---|---|---|
| body | unreadable JSON or wrong JSON types → only this error | `Request body is not valid JSON.` |
| `type` | missing or not `EXTERNAL`/`STUDENT` (D-13) → only this error | `Registration type must be EXTERNAL or STUDENT.` |
| `firstName`, `lastName`, `email`, and `organization` (EXTERNAL) or `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme`, `studentId` (STUDENT) | trimmed (`String.strip()`, BR-02); null/empty after trim → required; longer than 200 (email 254) code points → too long (D-12) | `This field is required.` / `This value is too long.` |
| `email` | after trim must match `^[A-Za-z0-9.!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{\|}~-]+@[A-Za-z0-9](?:[A-Za-z0-9-]{0,61}[A-Za-z0-9])?(?:\.[A-Za-z0-9](?:[A-Za-z0-9-]{0,61}[A-Za-z0-9])?)+$` (BR-03; no whitespace, CR or LF) | `Enter a valid email address.` |
| fields of the other type | ignored, stored as null | — |
| `options` | null = none; an id listed twice (OQ-04), unknown, inactive (BR-04, SR-04) or not available to the type (OQ-01) → one error naming the first offending id | `Option '<id>' is not available.` / `Option '<id>' is selected more than once.` |
| `consents` | a mandatory consent missing (BR-05) or an id not in the configuration (D-11); duplicates collapse | `Consent '<id>' is required.` / `Consent '<id>' is unknown.` |
| `captchaToken` | null/blank → required; otherwise `CaptchaVerifier.verify(token)` false → rejected; verified only when every other field is valid | `This field is required.` / `The reCAPTCHA check failed. Please try again.` |

Any error → HTTP 400 `{"errors":[…]}`, nothing stored, no email (AC-001-02..07, AC-002-02..06).

### `POST /api/registrations` — acceptance flow (AR-05, BR-07, OQ-03)
1. `RegisterParticipant` validates and verifies the captcha.
2. `RegistrationStorage.store` (`@Transactional`): creates `Registration` (UUID, `registeredAt` = now truncated to milliseconds UTC, every given consent with `givenAt = registeredAt`), saves it through `RegistrationRepository` and flushes, then `JsonCopyStore.write` serialises it to [`registration-copy.schema.json`](02_contracts/registration-copy.schema.json) and writes `<id>.json` (temp file in the same directory, then atomic move). An exception rolls the row back; a rollback after the file was written deletes the file (transaction synchronisation). Any storage failure → `StorageFailedException` → HTTP 500 `{"message":"The registration could not be stored. Please try again later."}` (AC-005-03).
3. After the commit, `RegistrationNotifier` sends the participant confirmation and one organizer notification per address ([`emails.json`](02_contracts/emails.json)), synchronously with 5 s timeouts; each failure is caught and logged as `Email for registration <id> failed` only (no personal data, ES-07).
4. HTTP 201 `{"id":"<uuid>"}` with `Location`.

### `GET /api/export` (BR-08, US-008)
`ExportRegistrations` reads every registration ordered by `registeredAt`, `id`; `adapter.export.PoiWorkbookWriter` writes an XSSF workbook, sheet `Registrations`, header row of the 12 contract columns, one row per registration, all string cells (no formula evaluation of user text), `options`/`consents` joined by `, `, non-applicable cells empty, `registeredAt` as `Instant.toString()`. `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="registrations.xlsx"`.

### Errors (SB-07, ES-07)
`ApiExceptionHandler`: 400 as above; 404/405/415 and every unexpected exception → `{"message": "<generic text>"}` without stack traces, class names or SQL; Spring's whitelabel and `server.error.include-*` disabled. Log lines carry the registration id or request path, never field values.

## 5. Security (SB-01..SB-11, SR-01..SR-08, ASVS 5.0 L1)

- **Organizer access (SB-02, BR-08, SR-06, SR-07)**: Spring Security, stateless, HTTP Basic with one in-memory user (`ROLE_ORGANIZER`, BCrypt hash, SB-03). `/api/export` requires the role; `GET /api/form-config`, `POST /api/registrations`, `GET /actuator/health/**` are public; everything else is denied. Wrong or missing credentials → 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="organizer"` and no body data. `OrganizerHttpsOnlyFilter` runs after authentication on `/api/export`: when `https-only` is on, the request is not secure (`request.isSecure()`, with `server.forward-headers-strategy=native` honouring `X-Forwarded-Proto` from trusted internal proxies) and the client address is not loopback → 403 `{"message":"Organizer access requires HTTPS."}`, no data (AC-008-04). CSRF is disabled (no cookies or sessions; Basic credentials are not sent automatically cross-site by the form).
- **reCAPTCHA (SR-01, SR-02, DoD-P05)**: [`recaptcha.json`](02_contracts/recaptcha.json). `adapter.captcha.TestModeCaptchaVerifier` (token `test-pass`) or `GoogleCaptchaVerifier` (Spring `RestClient`, form POST to `app.captcha.verify-url`) selected by `app.captcha.test-mode`; the Google path is tested against a mock HTTP server, accepted and rejected token.
- **Rate and size limits (SR-03, SB-06)**: `RateLimitFilter` — fixed one-minute window per (client address, endpoint `METHOD path`) for every `/api/**` request, including failed logins; over the limit → 429 with `Retry-After`; old windows evicted. Client address = `request.getRemoteAddr()` after the native forward-header handling. `RequestSizeFilter` — `Content-Length` above `max-bytes` → 413; bodies without a length are read through a counting stream that fails at the limit → 413.
- **Input and output (SB-01, SB-05, SR-04, SR-05)**: server-side validation above; JPA with bound parameters; option ids checked against the active set; emails plain text, fixed subjects, no user text in headers; the export writes string cells.
- **Headers (SB-10)**: backend — `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `Cache-Control: no-store`. Frontend nginx — `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://www.google.com/recaptcha/ https://www.gstatic.com/recaptcha/; frame-src https://www.google.com/recaptcha/ https://recaptcha.google.com/recaptcha/; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, plus `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: same-origin`; `server_tokens off`. (`'unsafe-inline'` for styles only: the reCAPTCHA widget sets inline styles.)
- **CORS**: none by default; `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN` (local only) allows that origin for `/api/**` GET/POST.
- **TLS (SB-04)**: outside the machine through the external reverse proxy (`environments.md`); organizer access enforced as above.
- **Least privilege (SB-11)**: both images run as non-root users; the database user owns only its database.
- **Secrets (SB-03, ES-02)**: only from the environment / `.env`; no defaults in code; `.env` git-ignored.
- **Scanning (SB-08, SB-09)**: Dependency-Check, `npm audit`, Semgrep, Gitleaks, SpotBugs, PMD in phase 6.
- **Personal data (SB-12..SB-14)**: exactly the fields of `security-requirements.md` "Personal data"; retention OQ-06 (operator deletes rows and copies at most 12 months after the conference, stated in the release notes); consents never preselected, stored with `givenAt`.

## 6. Storage (BR-07, AR-06, ES-08, NFR-01)

[`database.json`](02_contracts/database.json): Flyway migration `V1__create_registration_tables.sql`; `spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=validate`. JPA entity `RegistrationEntity` with element collections for options (ordered) and consents. Database encoding UTF8; the JSON copy is UTF-8 written by Jackson; mails UTF-8; POI strings are Unicode — Slovenian characters survive every step.

## 7. Frontend (US-001..US-004, NFR-03, AR-01, AR-07)

| Module | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `src/api/client.ts` | `fetchFormConfig()`, `submitRegistration(payload)` → `{kind:'created',id} \| {kind:'invalid',errors} \| {kind:'failed'}`; relative `/api/...` URLs only |

| `src/components/OptionGroups.tsx`, `Captcha.tsx`, `Confirmation.tsx` | as named |
| `src/App.tsx` | loads the configuration, shows loading/error, form or confirmation |

## 4. REST API (AR-09, `api-contract.md`)

Exactly [`openapi.json`](02_contracts/openapi.json). Responses carry `Content-Type: application/json;charset=UTF-8` (`server.servlet.encoding.force-response=true`).

### `GET /api/form-config`
Active options only, each with `id`, `name`, `category`, `availableTo` (AC-003-01); all consents; `captchaSiteKey`; additional field `captchaTestMode`.

### `POST /api/registrations` — validation (`domain.RegistrationValidator`, SB-01)
All checks run and every failing field gets one entry (first failing rule per field), so the frontend can show them together.

| Field | Rule (in order) | Message |
|---|---|---|
| body | unreadable JSON or wrong JSON types → only this error | `Request body is not valid JSON.` |
| `type` | missing or not `EXTERNAL`/`STUDENT` (D-13) → only this error | `Registration type must be EXTERNAL or STUDENT.` |
| `firstName`, `lastName`, `email`, and `organization` (EXTERNAL) or `studyInstitution`, `studyProgramme`, `studentId` (STUDENT) | trimmed (`String.strip()`, BR-02); null/empty after trim → required; longer than 200 (email 254) code points → too long (D-12) | `This field is required.` / `This value is too long.` |
| `email` | after trim must match `^[A-Za-z0-9.!#$%&'*+/=?^_`{\|}~-]+@[A-Za-z0-9](?:[A-Za-z0-9-]{0,61}[A-Za-z0-9])?(?:\.[A-Za-z0-9](?:[A-Za-z0-9-]{0,61}[A-Za-z0-9])?)+$` (BR-03; no whitespace, CR or LF) | `Enter a valid email address.` |
| fields of the other type | ignored, stored as null | — |
| `options` | null = none; an id listed twice (OQ-04), unknown, inactive (BR-04, SR-04) or not available to the type (OQ-01) → one error naming the first offending id | `Option '<id>' is not available.` / `Option '<id>' is selected more than once.` |
| `consents` | a mandatory consent missing (BR-05) or an id not in the configuration (D-11); duplicates collapse | `Consent '<id>' is required.` / `Consent '<id>' is unknown.` |
| `captchaToken` | null/blank → required; otherwise `CaptchaVerifier.verify(token)` false → rejected; verified only when every other field is valid | `This field is required.` / `The reCAPTCHA check failed. Please try again.` |

Any error → HTTP 400 `{"errors":[…]}`, nothing stored, no email (AC-001-02..07, AC-002-02..06).

### `POST /api/registrations` — acceptance flow (AR-05, BR-07, OQ-03)
1. `RegisterParticipant` validates and verifies the captcha.
2. `RegistrationStorage.store` (`@Transactional`): creates `Registration` (UUID, `registeredAt` = now truncated to milliseconds UTC, every given consent with `givenAt = registeredAt`), saves it through `RegistrationRepository` and flushes, then `JsonCopyStore.write` serialises it to [`registration-copy.schema.json`](02_contracts/registration-copy.schema.json) and writes `<id>.json` (temp file in the same directory, then atomic move). An exception rolls the row back; a rollback after the file was written deletes the file (transaction synchronisation). Any storage failure → `StorageFailedException` → HTTP 500 `{"message":"The registration could not be stored. Please try again later."}` (AC-005-03).
3. After the commit, `RegistrationNotifier` sends the participant confirmation and one organizer notification per address ([`emails.json`](02_contracts/emails.json)), synchronously with 5 s timeouts; each failure is caught and logged as `Email for registration <id> failed` only (no personal data, ES-07).
4. HTTP 201 `{"id":"<uuid>"}` with `Location`.

### `GET /api/export` (BR-08, US-008)
`ExportRegistrations` reads every registration ordered by `registeredAt`, `id`; `adapter.export.PoiWorkbookWriter` writes an XSSF workbook, sheet `Registrations`, header row of the 12 contract columns, one row per registration, all string cells (no formula evaluation of user text), `options`/`consents` joined by `, `, non-applicable cells empty, `registeredAt` as `Instant.toString()`. `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="registrations.xlsx"`.

### Errors (SB-07, ES-07)
`ApiExceptionHandler`: 400 as above; 404/405/415 and every unexpected exception → `{"message": "<generic text>"}` without stack traces, class names or SQL; Spring's whitelabel and `server.error.include-*` disabled. Log lines carry the registration id or request path, never field values.

## 5. Security (SB-01..SB-11, SR-01..SR-08, ASVS 5.0 L1)

- **Organizer access (SB-02, BR-08, SR-06, SR-07)**: Spring Security, stateless, HTTP Basic with one in-memory user (`ROLE_ORGANIZER`, BCrypt hash, SB-03). `/api/export` requires the role; `GET /api/form-config`, `POST /api/registrations`, `GET /actuator/health/**` are public; everything else is denied. Wrong or missing credentials → 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="organizer"` and no body data. `OrganizerHttpsOnlyFilter` runs after authentication on `/api/export`: when `https-only` is on, the request is not secure (`request.isSecure()`, with `server.forward-headers-strategy=native` honouring `X-Forwarded-Proto` from trusted internal proxies) and the client address is not loopback → 403 `{"message":"Organizer access requires HTTPS."}`, no data (AC-008-04). CSRF is disabled (no cookies or sessions; Basic credentials are not sent automatically cross-site by the form).
- **reCAPTCHA (SR-01, SR-02, DoD-P05)**: [`recaptcha.json`](02_contracts/recaptcha.json). `adapter.captcha.TestModeCaptchaVerifier` (token `test-pass`) or `GoogleCaptchaVerifier` (Spring `RestClient`, form POST to `app.captcha.verify-url`) selected by `app.captcha.test-mode`; the Google path is tested against a mock HTTP server, accepted and rejected token.
- **Rate and size limits (SR-03, SB-06)**: `RateLimitFilter` — fixed one-minute window per (client address, endpoint `METHOD path`) for every `/api/**` request, including failed logins; over the limit → 429 with `Retry-After`; old windows evicted. Client address = `request.getRemoteAddr()` after the native forward-header handling. `RequestSizeFilter` — `Content-Length` above `max-bytes` → 413; bodies without a length are read through a counting stream that fails at the limit → 413.
- **Input and output (SB-01, SB-05, SR-04, SR-05)**: server-side validation above; JPA with bound parameters; option ids checked against the active set; emails plain text, fixed subjects, no user text in headers; the export writes string cells.
- **Headers (SB-10)**: backend — `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `Cache-Control: no-store`. Frontend nginx — `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://www.google.com/recaptcha/ https://www.gstatic.com/recaptcha/; frame-src https://www.google.com/recaptcha/ https://recaptcha.google.com/recaptcha/; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, plus `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: same-origin`; `server_tokens off`. (`'unsafe-inline'` for styles only: the reCAPTCHA widget sets inline styles.)
- **CORS**: none by default; `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN` (local only) allows that origin for `/api/**` GET/POST.
- **TLS (SB-04)**: outside the machine through the external reverse proxy (`environments.md`); organizer access enforced as above.
- **Least privilege (SB-11)**: both images run as non-root users; the database user owns only its database.
- **Secrets (SB-03, ES-02)**: only from the environment / `.env`; no defaults in code; `.env` git-ignored.
- **Scanning (SB-08, SB-09)**: Dependency-Check, `npm audit`, Semgrep, Gitleaks, SpotBugs, PMD in phase 6.
- **Personal data (SB-12..SB-14)**: exactly the fields of `security-requirements.md` "Personal data"; retention OQ-06 (operator deletes rows and copies at most 12 months after the conference, stated in the release notes); consents never preselected, stored with `givenAt`.

## 6. Storage (BR-07, AR-06, ES-08, NFR-01)

[`database.json`](02_contracts/database.json): Flyway migration `V1__create_registration_tables.sql`; `spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=validate`. JPA entity `RegistrationEntity` with element collections for options (ordered) and consents. Database encoding UTF8; the JSON copy is UTF-8 written by Jackson; mails UTF-8; POI strings are Unicode — Slovenian characters survive every step.

## 7. Frontend (US-001..US-004, NFR-03, AR-01, AR-07)

React 19 single page following [`ui-registration-form.json`](02_contracts/ui-registration-form.json).

| Module | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `src/api/client.ts` | `fetchFormConfig()`, `submitRegistration(payload)` → `{kind:'created',id} \| {kind:'invalid',errors} \| {kind:'failed'}`; relative `/api/...` URLs only |
| `src/domain/validation.ts` | client rules mirroring section 4 (required after trim, email pattern, lengths, mandatory consents, captcha) |
| `src/domain/payload.ts` | builds the request: trimmed values, only the fields of the chosen type, selected option ids in display order, consent ids, token |
| `src/components/RegistrationForm.tsx` | type chooser, fields, option groups, consents, captcha, submit, field and general errors |
| `src/components/OptionGroups.tsx`, `Captcha.tsx`, `Confirmation.tsx` | as named |
| `src/App.tsx` | loads the configuration, shows loading/error, form or confirmation |

Behaviour: no type chosen → only the chooser; choosing a type shows exactly that type's fields and the active options available to it grouped by category (AC-001-08, AC-002-07); client validation blocks the request (AC-004-03); 400 → backend errors next to fields, values kept (AC-004-02); 201 → confirmation with the participant's name and selected option names, form removed (AC-004-01); other status or network error → general error, no details (AC-004-04). +- **Rate and size limits (SR-03, SB-06)**: `RateLimitFilter` — fixed one-minute window per (client address, endpoint `METHOD path`) for every `/api/**` request, including failed logins; over the limit → 429 with `Retry-After`; old windows evicted. Client address = `request.getRemoteAddr()` after the native forward-header handling. `RequestSizeFilter` — `Content-Length` above `max-bytes` → 413; bodies without a length are read through a counting stream that fails at the limit → 413.

+- **Input and output (SB-01, SB-05, SR-04, SR-05)**: server-side validation above; JPA with bound parameters; option ids checked against the active set; emails plain text, fixed subjects, no user text in headers; the export writes string cells.

+- **Headers (SB-10)**: backend — `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, `Cache-Control: no-store`. Frontend nginx — `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://www.google.com/recaptcha/ https://www.gstatic.com/recaptcha/; frame-src https://www.google.com/recaptcha/ https://recaptcha.google.com/recaptcha/; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, plus `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: same-origin`; `server_tokens off`. (`'unsafe-inline'` for styles only: the reCAPTCHA widget sets inline styles.)
+- **CORS**: none by default; `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN` (local only) allows that origin for `/api/**` GET/POST.
+- **TLS (SB-04)**: outside the machine through the external reverse proxy (`environments.md`); organizer access enforced as above.
+- **Least privilege (SB-11)**: both images run as non-root users; the database user owns only its database.
+- **Secrets (SB-03, ES-02)**: only from the environment / `.env`; no defaults in code; `.env` git-ignored.
+- **Scanning (SB-08, SB-09)**: Dependency-Check, `npm audit`, Semgrep, Gitleaks, SpotBugs, PMD in phase 6.

+- **Personal data (SB-12..SB-14)**: exactly the fields of `security-requirements.md` "Personal data"; retention OQ-06 (operator deletes rows and copies at most 12 months after the conference, stated in the release notes); consents never preselected, stored with `givenAt`.

+[`database.json`](02_contracts/database.json): Flyway migration `V1__create_registration_tables.sql`; `spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=validate`. JPA entity `RegistrationEntity` with element collections for options (ordered) and consents. Database encoding UTF8; the JSON copy is UTF-8 written by Jackson; mails UTF-8; POI strings are Unicode — Slovenian characters survive every step.
+| `src/domain/validation.ts` | client rules mirroring section 4 (required after trim, email pattern, lengths, mandatory consents, captcha) |
+| `src/domain/payload.ts` | builds the request: trimmed values, only the fields of the chosen type, selected option ids in display order, consent ids, token |
+| `src/components/RegistrationForm.tsx` | type chooser, fields, option groups, consents, captcha, submit, field and general errors |
+| `src/App.tsx` | loads the configuration, shows loading/error, form or confirmation |

+Behaviour: no type chosen → only the chooser; choosing a type shows exactly that type's fields and the active options available to it grouped by category (AC-001-08, AC-002-07); client validation blocks the request (AC-004-03); 400 → backend errors next to fields, values kept (AC-004-02); 201 → confirmation with the participant's name and selected option names, form removed (AC-004-01); other status or network error → general error, no details (AC-004-04). # Local stack: backend, frontend, PostgreSQL and Mailpit on 127.0.0.1 only (environments.md).
# Start from 02_output/ with: docker compose --env-file ../.env up -d --build
name: registration

services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:16.15-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: registration
      POSTGRES_USER: registration
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env}
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "pg_isready", "-U", "registration", "-d", "registration"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 20
    restart: unless-stopped

  mailpit:
    image: axllent/mailpit:v1.31.1
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8025:8025"
    restart: unless-stopped

  backend:
    build: ./backend
    environment:
      SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE: local
      DB_URL: jdbc:postgresql://postgres:5432/registration
      DB_USERNAME: registration
      DB_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env}
      MAIL_HOST: mailpit
      MAIL_PORT: "1025"
      MAIL_TLS: "false"
      MAIL_FROM: ${MAIL_FROM:-registration@konferenca.example}
      CONFERENCE_NAME: ${CONFERENCE_NAME:-Konferenca 2026}
      JSON_COPY_DIR: /data/json-copies
      CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE: ${CAPTCHA_TEST_MODE:-true}
      RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY: ${RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY:-}
      RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY: ${RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY:-}
      ORGANIZER_USERNAME: ${ORGANIZER_USERNAME:?set ORGANIZER_USERNAME in .env}
      ORGANIZER_PASSWORD: ${ORGANIZER_PASSWORD:?set ORGANIZER_PASSWORD in .env}
      ORGANIZER_EMAILS: ${ORGANIZER_EMAILS:?set ORGANIZER_EMAILS in .env}
      ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY: ${ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY:-false}
      RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE: ${RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE:-30}
    volumes:
      - json-copies:/data/json-copies
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8080:8080"
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      mailpit:
        condition: service_started
    restart: unless-stopped

  frontend:
    build: ./frontend
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:3000:8080"
    depends_on:
      backend:
        condition: service_healthy
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  pgdata:
  json-copies:
